content_html:
<p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5"># 狗狗營養缺乏症完整指南 — 症狀識別與補充方法</p><h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-near-black mt-10 mb-3">前言：為何自煮鮮食容易出現營養失衡？</h2><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">很多狗主人都會為毛孩親手準備鮮食，覺得這樣既健康又安心。但你知道嗎？自製鮮食其實暗藏營養陷阱！根據研究，<strong>高達九成自製狗糧都存在營養不均的問題</strong>，尤其是一些關鍵維生素和礦物質的缺乏。</p><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">這不是要嚇唬你，而是想提醒你：了解營養缺乏的症狀和正確的補充方法，才能讓你的愛犬真正食得健康。</p>

title_en: The Complete Guide to Nutritional Deficiencies in Dogs — Symptoms and How to Fix Them
desc_en: Up to 90% of homemade dog food is nutritionally unbalanced. A vet-style breakdown of the key deficiencies, the symptoms to watch for, and the right way to supplement them.
content_html_en:
Short answer: Most homemade dog diets are missing one or more key nutrients. Knowing which deficiencies show up as which symptoms is the difference between guessing and actually fixing the problem.

Why is homemade food so easy to get wrong?

Plenty of owners cook for their dogs because it feels healthier and safer than kibble. That's a fair instinct. But research puts the share of nutritionally unbalanced homemade dog diets at around 90% — almost always because the recipe skips one or more of the micronutrients dogs can't live without: key vitamins and minerals.

The point isn't to scare you off home cooking. It's to give you a working vocabulary: what deficiency looks like, which nutrients are most often missing, and how to fill the gaps without overdoing it.

content_html:
<p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5"># 狗狗家居按摩治療基礎 — 放鬆肌肉與促進血液循環</p><h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-near-black mt-10 mb-3">為什麼你的狗狗需要按摩？</h2><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">你有冇試過放工返到屋企，成身攰到想攤喺梳化唔郁？其實你嘅狗狗都一樣會有身體疲勞同肌肉繃緊嘅時候。不過佢哋唔識得用說話話俾我哋知，只係會用行為表達——例如唔願郁、行路姿勢奇怪、或者成日舔某個部位。</p><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">近年獸醫學發展得好快，狗狗嘅壽命比20年前長咗足足兩倍。但壽命長咗，伴隨而嚟嘅就係各種老年病——心衰竭、腎衰竭、關節炎、糖尿病……呢啲慢性病好多時西醫都只能控制，而唔係根治。加上手術同藥物嘅副作用，令愈來愈多主人開始為毛孩尋找更溫和嘅輔助療法。</p><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">寵物按摩就係其中一種。佢唔係要取代正規獸醫治療，而係作為一種<strong>補充療法</strong>，幫助狗狗放鬆肌肉、促進血液循環、增強免疫力，同時仲可以增進你同狗狗之間嘅感情。</p><h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-near-black mt-10 mb-3">按摩對狗狗嘅12大好處</h2><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">我哋先講啲實際嘅好處，等你明白點解要學呢門手藝：</p><div class="overflow-x-auto my-3"><table class="w-full text-sm border-collapse"><tr><th class="border border-gray-100 px-3 py-2.5 bg-brand-light text-brand font-semibold text-left">好處</th><th class="border border-gray-100 px-3 py-2.5 bg-brand-light text-brand font-semibold text-left">具體效果</th><th class="border border-gray-100 px-3 py-2.5 bg-brand-light text-brand font-semibold text-left">點樣幫到狗狗</th></tr><tr></tr></table></div>

title_en: Home Massage Therapy for Dogs — Relaxing Muscles and Boosting Circulation
desc_en: Canine massage works alongside vet care to ease muscle tension, improve circulation, and strengthen the bond with your dog. Here's how to do it safely at home.
content_html_en:
Short answer: Dogs carry muscle tension and fatigue just like we do — they just can't tell us in words. A few minutes of massage a day relaxes tight muscles, improves circulation, and quietly strengthens the bond between you.

Why does your dog actually need massage?

You've had those days — finish work, get home, every muscle is screaming for the sofa. Your dog has them too. They just can't say it. Instead you see it in their behaviour: reluctance to move, an odd gait, or constant licking at one spot.

Veterinary medicine has come a long way. Dogs today live roughly twice as long as they did 20 years ago. Longer life means more chronic conditions to manage — heart failure, kidney failure, arthritis, diabetes. Western medicine can often control these but rarely cure them, and surgery plus medication come with side effects. That's why more owners are looking for gentler supportive therapies alongside the vet's plan.

Canine massage is one of them. It isn't meant to replace vet treatment. It's a complementary therapy that helps relax tight muscles, promote blood flow, support the immune system, and — as a bonus — deepen the bond between you and your dog.

<p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5"># 狗狗鮮食營養指南 — 自煮鮮食的營養比例與食材選擇</p><h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-near-black mt-10 mb-3">前言：為什麼要為狗狗自煮鮮食？</h2><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">香港的寵物主人愈來愈重視毛孩的飲食健康，自煮鮮食已成為不少狗主的新選擇。然而，很多主人在開始自煮鮮食時，最常遇到的問題是：「究竟要落幾多肉？」、「點樣先算均衡？」、「狗狗食鮮食會唔會唔夠營養？」</p><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">其實，為狗狗準備鮮食，不單是將肉類和蔬菜隨便煮熟那麼簡單。一餐均衡的鮮食，需要考慮蛋白質、脂肪、碳水化合物、維生素和礦物質的適當比例。更重要的是，每隻狗狗的體質都不同，有些狗狗怕冷，有些容易皮膚敏感，有些腸胃較弱——這些都需要透過飲食來調整。</p><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">這篇文章會從現代營養學和中醫食療兩個角度，教你如何為狗狗設計均衡的鮮食餐單，讓毛孩食得健康又開心。</p>

title_en: The Dog Fresh-Food Nutrition Guide — Ratios, Ingredients, and a Balanced Plate
desc_en: Homemade dog food needs the right balance of protein, fat, carbs, vitamins, and minerals — not just cooked meat and veg. A practical guide for HK owners.
content_html_en:
Short answer: Cooking for your dog isn't just meat plus vegetables. A balanced fresh meal needs the right ratio of protein, fat, carbs, vitamins, and minerals — and that ratio shifts with your dog's body type and condition.

Why cook fresh food for your dog?

Hong Kong owners are paying closer attention to what goes into the bowl, and homemade fresh food has become a real alternative to commercial kibble. The questions that come up the moment you start are always the same: how much meat? How do I know it's balanced? Will my dog miss something by not eating kibble?

Cooking fresh food isn't just a matter of boiling some meat and veg together. A balanced meal needs the right ratio of protein, fat, carbohydrate, vitamins, and minerals. On top of that, every dog is different — some run cold, some have sensitive skin, some have a delicate stomach. Diet should respond to all of that.

This guide walks through both modern nutrition and traditional Chinese food therapy, so you can build a fresh-food menu that keeps your dog healthy and happy at the bowl.

<p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5"># 狗隻中醫五元素養生法 — 體質辨識與食療調理</p><h2 class="text-xl font-bold text-near-black mt-10 mb-3">前言：為什麼要從中醫角度照顧狗狗？</h2><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">你有冇試過，狗狗明明食足三餐、營養均衡，但依然皮毛乾燥、精神不振、成日病？或者，你已經好努力跟足網上食譜整鮮食，但狗狗嘅身體狀況始終冇乜改善？</p><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">其實，問題可能唔係「食得唔夠」，而係「食得唔啱體質」。</p><p class="text-base text-gray-700 leading-8 mb-5">中醫養生嘅核心，係講求「整體平衡」。人同狗一樣，身體狀況會隨季節、年齡、情緒同飲食而變化。今日，我哋就用一個全新角度——<strong>中醫五元素（五行）養生法</strong>，幫你了解狗狗嘅體質，再透過日常飲食，由內到外調理好佢哋嘅身體。</p>

參考文獻

title_en: The Five Elements (Wu Xing) Approach to Canine Wellness — Body Type and Food Therapy
desc_en: TCM Five Elements is a framework for reading your dog's body type and tuning the diet to it. A practical primer on Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, and Water dogs.
content_html_en:
Short answer: Some dogs eat well and stay dull and itchy. The Five Elements framework reads your dog as a body type — Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, or Water — and lets you tune the diet and lifestyle to the type, not just to the ingredient list.

Why take a TCM angle on dog care?

Have you ever had a dog who eats three proper meals a day, gets a balanced diet, and still looks dull-coated, low-energy, and constantly a bit under the weather? Or you've followed a fresh-food recipe to the letter and your dog just… doesn't really improve.

Most of the time the problem isn't "not enough food" — it's "not the right food for this particular dog."

Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) thinks in terms of whole-body balance. Dogs and humans are alike in this: body condition shifts with season, age, mood, and diet. Today we're going to use one framework — the Five Elements (Wu Xing) — to read your dog's body type and then dial in the everyday diet to support them from the inside out.

title_en: The Dog First-Aid & Emergency Handbook — What to Do in the Golden Hour
desc_en: From choking and heatstroke to cuts and poisoning — a clear step-by-step guide to the home accidents HK owners see most often, and how to stabilise your dog before reaching the vet.
content_html_en:
Short answer: A choking dog, a heatstroke dog, a dog that's eaten something it shouldn't have — the first ten minutes decide a lot. A simple, memorised emergency flow beats panicking every time.

This handbook reorganises the course notes into a fresh, original read for Hong Kong dog owners — practical everyday wording, the common home accidents HK dogs actually get into, and a clear emergency flow you can run through in your head before you reach the clinic.

Every dog owner dreads the moment something goes wrong at home — a curious bite, a play injury gone too far, a hot day that turns into heatstroke. These things don't wait for office hours. The fix isn't panic; it's preparation. Knowing a clean emergency flow means you stay steady in the golden minutes and give your dog the best chance while you get to the vet.

This guide breaks the most common home emergencies down step by step, in plain language, so you don't have to think too hard in the moment. We start with the accidents owners see most, then walk through the response.

title: 狗食物過敏致敏排行榜與排除飲食指南
source: 改編自 Mueller RS 等 (2016) BMC Vet Res 研究 + Dogalicious 實證整理
disclaimer: 本文內容整理自學術文獻與公開資料，經重新編寫加入原創分析。如有健康問題請諮詢註冊獸醫。排除飲食應在獸醫指導下進行。
content_html:
一句話重點：狗食物過敏要靠排除飲食確診，而非驗血或驗唾液——選一種全新蛋白，嚴格餵八週，再在獸醫指導下逐一重新挑戰。

致敏排行榜

一項針對犬隻皮膚型食物不良反應（CAFR）嘅回顧，整理咗 297 隻確診狗嘅資料，得出呢個排行榜：

排名致敏來源個案百分比
🥇牛肉10234%
🥈奶製品5117%
🥉雞肉4515%
4小麥3813%
5大豆186%
6羊肉145%
7粟米134%
8蛋114%
9豬肉72%
10魚52%
11米52%

唔係「牛肉有害」，而係「接觸得多」

呢個排行榜最容易被誤讀嘅地方，係將佢當成毒性排名。佢唔係。

食物過敏需要免疫系統先「認識」一種蛋白，先會對佢產生反應。同一種蛋白食得越多、食得越耐，被認住嘅機會就越高。牛肉同雞肉之所以位居榜首，正因為佢哋係市面上最普遍嘅狗糧蛋白——而唔係佢哋本身有問題。

呢個就係新穎蛋白（novel protein）嘅邏輯：揀一款你隻狗幾乎未食過嘅蛋白，令佢嘅免疫系統冇機會學會對佢反應。豬肉、魚、火雞、鹿肉、袋鼠肉都屬於呢類。

狗食物過敏係點樣形成嘅

狗食物過敏係免疫系統對食物中一種蛋白產生嘅反應——通常係一種中至大分子嘅醣蛋白，被免疫系統誤認為威脅。當中同時牽涉抗體介導與細胞介導嘅途徑，所以症狀可能喺進食後數小時甚至數日先出現。

呢個機制帶出兩個重要原則：

  • 必須曾經接觸 — 狗唔可能對從未食過嘅蛋白過敏。過敏往往是對熟悉嘅食物形成，而唔係對稀奇嘅食物。
  • 反應延遲而且會累積 — 由於部分屬細胞介導，今日偷食一次，可能到本週稍後先發作，呢個就係點解需要一個乾淨嘅試驗窗口。

分辨三個概念

  • 食物過敏 — 免疫系統對蛋白嘅反應，常見於皮膚與耳朵痕癢，有時伴腸胃症狀。只能靠排除飲食診斷。
  • 食物不耐受 — 非免疫性反應，例如難以消化高脂食材，通常只有腸胃症狀（軟便、脹氣）。
  • 環境過敏（異位性皮膚炎） — 對花粉、塵蟎或霉菌嘅反應，與食物無關，表現可以一模一樣。

排除飲食：八週逐週拆解

  1. 第 1–2 週：過渡與建立基線。皮膚未必有變化——你係喺清空系統，唔係期待奇蹟。
  2. 第 3–5 週：若食物係誘因，痕癢分數與耳炎通常開始緩和。
  3. 第 6–8 週：最清晰嘅判讀期。要嚴格記錄每週變化。
  4. 重新挑戰：加返舊糧，若 1-2 週內痕癢重現，診斷即告成立。

⚠️ 嚴格嘅開始：除咗試驗糧，唔可以俾任何其他蛋白來源——零食、潔齒骨、加味保健品、人類食物、朋友俾嘅火腿，全部要停。一粒芝士就足以令整個測試失效。

香港嘅現實

香港溫暖潮濕嘅氣候令皮膚屏障全年受壓，並助長繼發性酵母菌與細菌感染——狗狗嘅皮膚幾乎冇「淡季」可以復元。加上我哋嘅飲食文化習慣共享飯菜，嚴格的八週試驗需要真正的紀律。

title_en: Dog Food Allergy Rankings & Elimination Diet Guide — What the 2016 Mueller Study Actually Shows
desc_en: Beef, dairy, chicken top the list — not because they're toxic, but because dogs meet them most often. How to read the rankings and run a proper 8-week elimination diet.
content_html_en:
Short answer: Dog food allergy has to be diagnosed with an elimination diet, not a blood or saliva test. Pick one novel protein, feed it strictly for eight weeks, then — under vet supervision — challenge the old foods one at a time.

The allergen rankings

A review of canine cutaneous adverse food reactions (CAFR) pulled together data from 297 confirmed cases. Here's the ranking that came out:

RankAllergenCasesShare
🥇Beef10234%
🥈Dairy5117%
🥉Chicken4515%
4Wheat3813%
5Soy186%
6Lamb145%
7Corn134%
8Egg114%
9Pork72%
10Fish52%
11Rice52%

Not "beef is bad" — it's "exposure is high"

The most common way to misread this chart is to treat it like a toxicity ranking. It isn't.

Food allergy needs the immune system to first recognise a protein before it can react to it. The longer and more often your dog has eaten a protein, the more chances the immune system has to learn it. Beef and chicken sit at the top precisely because they're the most common proteins in commercial dog food — not because the proteins themselves are in any way harmful.

This is exactly the logic behind a novel protein: pick something your dog has barely or never eaten, so the immune system has had no chance to learn it. Pork, fish, turkey, venison, and kangaroo all fit that bucket.

How a dog food allergy actually forms

A canine food allergy is the immune system reacting to a protein in the food — usually a medium- to large-sized glycoprotein that the immune system mistakes for a threat. Both antibody-mediated and cell-mediated pathways are involved, which is why symptoms can show up hours or even days after a meal.

Two important principles follow from that:

  • Prior exposure is required. A dog cannot react to a protein it has never eaten. Allergies tend to develop against familiar foods, not exotic ones.
  • The reaction is delayed and cumulative. Because part of the response is cell-mediated, a single slip-up today may only flare later in the week — which is exactly why you need a clean testing window.

Three terms people mix up

  • Food allergy — immune reaction to a protein. Most often shows up as skin and ear itch, sometimes with gut symptoms. Can only be diagnosed with an elimination diet.
  • Food intolerance — non-immune, e.g. trouble digesting a high-fat food. Usually gut-only (loose stool, gas).
  • Environmental allergy (atopic dermatitis) — reaction to pollen, dust mites, or mould. Nothing to do with food, but the symptoms can look identical.

The elimination diet: 8 weeks, week by week

  1. Weeks 1–2: transition and baseline. The skin may not change — you're clearing the system, not expecting a miracle yet.
  2. Weeks 3–5: if food is the trigger, itch scores and ear infections usually start to ease.
  3. Weeks 6–8: the cleanest read. Track changes weekly.
  4. Re-challenge: reintroduce the old food. If the itch returns within 1–2 weeks, the diagnosis is locked in.

⚠️ A strict start: beyond the test food, no other protein source — no treats, no dental chews, no flavoured supplements, no human food, no well-meaning ham from a friend. A single cube of cheese is enough to invalidate the whole trial.

The Hong Kong reality

Hong Kong's warm, humid climate puts the skin barrier under pressure year-round and helps secondary yeast and bacterial infections take hold — dogs here barely get a quiet season for the skin to recover. Add a food culture that shares meals at the table, and an honest eight-week trial takes real discipline.

References

  1. Mueller RS, Olivry T, Prélaud P. Critically appraised topic on adverse food reactions of companion animals (2): common food allergen sources in dogs and cats. BMC Vet Res. 2016;12:9.
  2. Olivry T, Mueller RS. Critically appraised topic on adverse food reactions of companion animals (3): prevalence of cutaneous adverse food reactions in dogs and cats. BMC Vet Res. 2017;13:51.
  3. Cutaneous Food Allergy in Animals. Merck Veterinary Manual.
  4. AAFCO. Pet Food Labeling Guidelines.
  5. FDA. Complete and Balanced Pet Food Definitions.

title: 狗狗口臭點算？獸醫話你知真正原因同解決方法
source: 參考：NIH PMC9074277, PMC10981081, PMC7472411, BluePearl Vet
disclaimer: 本文僅供參考，如狗狗口臭持續或嚴重，請務必諮詢獸醫。排除飲食應在獸醫指導下進行。
content_html:
一句話重點：狗狗口臭唔係正常嘅事——可能係牙周病、腎功能問題（BUN偏高）或者飲食唔適合嘅警號，要對症處理先有效。

口臭係點樣形成嘅？

根據NIH研究（PMC9074277），狗口臭主要係因為口腔內細菌分解含硫胺基酸（半胱氨酸同甲硫氨酸）時產生嘅揮發性硫化物（VSCs）。呢啲化合物就係我哋聞到嘅難聞氣味。

研究顯示，狗牙周病嘅患病率高達44%至100%，係小動物臨床最常見嘅疾病之一。但牙周病唔係唯一原因。

四大成因分析

1. 牙周病（最常見）🥇

牙菌斑同牙石積聚，滋生大量厭氧細菌產生硫化物。牙周病唔止影響口腔，細菌仲可以進入血液，引發心臟、腎臟等其他器官問題。

2. 腎臟問題（BUN偏高）⚠️

腎功能受損嘅狗，血液中尿素氮（BUN）會升高。尿素會透過呼吸排出，產生類似氨水或尿味嘅口氣——學術上叫「uremic breath」。如果口臭帶有阿摩尼亞味，要即時驗血check腎功能。

3. 高蛋白飲食 🥩

研究顯示（PMC7472411），高蛋白飲食會改變狗嘅腸道菌群，增加蛋白質分解細菌。部分代謝產物透過呼吸排出，令口氣變差。羊肉、袋鼠肉呢類高蛋白紅肉影響尤其明顯。

4. 消化問題

腸胃消化不良、食物過敏或寄生蟲感染都可能導致口臭。食物喺腸道腐敗產生嘅氣體反流到口腔，就會有酸餿味。

參考案例：點心嘅情況

點心（18kg）嘅情況好有參考價值：

  • BUN偏高（2025-09血檢）→ 腎臟負荷要留意
  • 主食羊肉+袋鼠肉乾糧 → 高蛋白紅肉，代謝負擔大
  • 口臭+口水都臭 → 可能係腎源性（阿摩尼亞味）混合高蛋白飲食嘅結果

建議：先檢查牙齒有冇牙石，同時驗血覆檢BUN/CREA，確認口臭來源。

實戰建議

🪥 刷牙（最有效）

每日用寵物專用牙膏牙刷，研究證實可以顯著減少口臭。千祈唔好用人的牙膏（含氟有毒）。

🥬 飲食調整

  • BUN偏高 → 考慮轉低磷低蛋白主食，減少羊肉/袋鼠肉比例
  • 加入新鮮巴西利（parsley）切碎混糧，天然除口臭
  • 冷壓椰子油半茶匙溝糧，月桂酸抗菌
  • 益生菌繼續（你已經有俾），改善腸道菌群
  • 增加飲水（多放水碗/寵物飲水機）稀釋BUN

🏥 定期檢查

如果口臭持續或突然變嚴重，要做血常規（BUN/CREA）同牙科檢查。尤其係阿摩尼亞味嘅口臭，可能係腎病警號。

香港本地化

潮濕天氣：香港嘅潮濕氣候令口腔細菌滋生更快，要更勤力清潔水兜同玩具。

鮮食文化：好多香港狗主餵鮮食，但要留意蛋白質比例。如果好似點心咁食開羊肉+袋鼠肉，可以考慮溝低蛋白肉類（火雞、兔肉），或增加蔬菜比例。

參考文獻

  1. Effectiveness of oral care interventions on malodour in dogs. NIH. PMC9074277.
  2. Effects of dental chew on halitosis in dogs. NIH. PMC10981081. 2024.
  3. Varying Protein Levels Influence Metabolomics and Gut Microbiota in Dogs. NIH. PMC7472411.
  4. Chronic Kidney Disease & Renal Failure. BluePearl Veterinary Partners.
title_en: Why Does My Dog Have Bad Breath? A Vet Explains the Real Causes and What Actually Helps
desc_en: Dog bad breath is a warning sign — dental disease, kidney issues (high BUN), or the wrong diet. A vet breaks down the four real causes and the fixes that work.
content_html_en:
Short answer: Dog bad breath is not normal. It usually points to dental disease, kidney trouble (BUN running high), or a diet that doesn't suit your dog. Treating the symptom alone won't work — you have to find the source.

How does the smell actually form?

NIH research (PMC9074277) traces most doggy breath to volatile sulfur compounds (VSCs). Anaerobic bacteria in the mouth break down sulfur-containing amino acids (cysteine and methionine) and release these gases as a byproduct. That's the smell.

Studies put the rate of canine periodontal disease somewhere between 44% and 100%. It's one of the most common conditions vets see in small-animal practice. But gum disease isn't the only thing that stinks up a dog's mouth.

The four real causes

1. Periodontal disease (most common) 🥇

Plaque hardens into tartar. Anaerobic bacteria thrive under the gumline and pump out sulfur compounds. The damage doesn't stop at the mouth either — those bacteria can slip into the bloodstream and trouble the heart and kidneys down the line.

2. Kidney trouble (BUN running high) ⚠️

When the kidneys aren't filtering properly, blood urea nitrogen (BUN) climbs. Urea finds its way out through the breath and gives an ammonia or urine-like smell — vets call this "uremic breath." If your dog's breath smells like ammonia, get bloodwork done. Don't wait.

3. A high-protein diet 🥩

A 2022 study (PMC7472411) showed that high-protein diets shift the gut microbiome and grow protein-fermenting bacteria. Some of those metabolites end up in the breath. Red meats like lamb and kangaroo make the effect worse.

4. Digestion problems

Indigestion, food allergies, or a parasite load can all push gas back up into the mouth. Rotting food in the gut gives off a sour smell that travels.

A real case: Dim Sum's situation

Dim Sum is an 18kg dog. The pattern here is useful:

  • BUN on the high side (Sept 2025 bloodwork) — kidneys are working harder than they should.
  • Main food is lamb + kangaroo kibble — high-protein red meat, which adds metabolic load.
  • Bad breath plus smelly saliva — likely a mix of kidney-origin ammonia and high-protein diet output.

Plan: check the teeth for tartar buildup, redo BUN and CREA on bloodwork, and figure out which factor is the bigger contributor.

What actually helps

🪥 Brushing (the single most effective thing)

Daily brushing with a pet-specific toothpaste and brush cuts bad breath significantly in trials. Never use human toothpaste — the fluoride is toxic to dogs.

🥬 Diet changes

  • If BUN is high, move toward a lower-phosphorus, lower-protein kibble and trim the lamb or kangaroo share.
  • Stir in fresh chopped parsley — a natural breath freshener.
  • A half-teaspoon of cold-pressed coconut oil mixed into the food adds lauric acid, which has antibacterial action.
  • Keep the probiotic going (if you're already giving one) to balance the gut.
  • Add more water stations or a pet drinking fountain — extra hydration dilutes BUN.

🏥 Routine checks

If bad breath sticks around or gets worse fast, run a full blood panel (BUN, CREA) and a dental exam. Ammonia-scented breath in particular can be a kidney warning sign.

Hong Kong specifics

Humidity: Hong Kong's damp climate lets oral bacteria multiply faster. Wash water bowls and chew toys more often than you would in a dry climate.

Fresh food culture: lots of HK owners feed home-cooked meals, which is great — but watch the protein ratio. If your dog is on lamb and kangaroo like Dim Sum, mix in leaner proteins (turkey, rabbit) or push the vegetable share higher.

FAQ

Is a little doggy breath normal?

Mild food-breath after a meal is one thing. A persistent foul smell is not. If you can smell it across the room, something's off.

Can dental chews replace brushing?

They help (NIH PMC10981081 showed measurable improvement in halitosis scores) but they don't substitute for actual brushing. Think of chews as a top-up, not the main event.

My dog's breath smells like ammonia. Is that an emergency?

Get bloodwork this week. Ammonia-scented breath is a textbook uremic-breath signal. If your dog is also lethargic, off food, or vomiting, that's an emergency clinic, not a wait-and-see.

Data sources

  2. Effects of dental chew on halitosis in dogs. NIH. PMC10981081. 2024.
  3. Varying Protein Levels Influence Metabolomics and Gut Microbiota in Dogs. NIH. PMC7472411.
  4. Chronic Kidney Disease & Renal Failure. BluePearl Veterinary Partners.

title: 狗狗腸胃健康完整指南：5 大警號大多數主人都錯過
tags: ['腸胃健康', '免疫力', '肚瀉', '脹氣', '皮膚痕癢', '食草', '益生菌']
source: 參考：Cornell Riney Canine Health Center, VCA Animal Hospitals, AAHA
disclaimer: 本文僅供參考。如狗狗出現持續肚瀉、嘔血、腹部脹大且精神差等情況，請立即求醫。
content_html:
一句話重點：狗狗約70%嘅免疫細胞住在腸道——腸胃唔止管消化，仲影響皮膚、精神和抵抗力。以下5個警號，大多數主人都錯過。

點解腸胃咁重要？

根據 Cornell Riney Canine Health Center，狗嘅腸胃道係全身最大嘅免疫器官——大約 70% 嘅免疫系統集中喺腸道。腸道菌群失衡唔單止引起肚瀉或者脹氣，仲會影響營養吸收、皮膚狀態同整體免疫力。

5 大腸胃警號

1. 便便異常 💩

持續肚瀉、便秘、或者便便顏色異常（黑色、帶血、橙黃色）都係腸胃求救訊號。偶爾一次軟便唔使慌，但連續幾日或者反覆出現就要留意。

2. 脹氣同肚脹 💨

排氣多可能係飲食問題或者菌群失衡。但腹部突然脹大、硬實、加上坐立不安同乾嘔，可能係胃扭轉（GDV）——呢個係即時致命急症，要即刻去獸醫院。

3. 皮膚痕癢、不停舔腳 🐾

腸胃問題經常「反映」喺皮膚——腸道發炎會令皮膚屏障變差，出現痕癢、紅疹同反覆耳部感染。如果皮膚問題點搽藥都唔好，不妨由腸胃入手。

4. 精神差、無曬力 ⚡

腸道吸收營養，吸收唔好就冇能量。如果狗狗長期易攰、運動冇癮，加上上面任何一個徵狀，腸胃健康值得 check 一 check。

5. 突然狂食草 🌱

研究顯示食草喺狗好常見，多數同補充纖維或者天性有關——少過 25% 狗食草後會嘔。但突然食草量大增，就可能係腸胃唔舒服嘅訊號，值得同獸醫傾下。

可以點做？

  • 高質飲食：穩定嘅優質蛋白同纖維，避免頻繁換糧
  • 循序漸進換糧：用 7-10 日慢慢過渡，減少腸胃壓力
  • 益生菌：獸醫認可嘅犬用益生菌可以幫助菌群平衡
  • 定期驅蟲：寄生蟲係腸胃問題常見原因
  • 出現 2 個或以上警號：帶狗狗做一次腸胃健康檢查

常見問題

Q：狗肚瀉幾耐先要睇獸醫？
成人狗肚瀉超過 24-48 小時、有血便、或者同時精神差／嘔，就應該求醫。幼犬例外——一旦肚瀉盡快睇。

Q：狗食草係咪腸胃有事？
通常唔係——多數係天性或者纖維需求。但突然食量大增就要留意。

Q：腹部脹大點樣算急症？
肚子又脹又硬、坐立不安、乾嘔但嘔唔出——好可能係胃扭轉（GDV），每分鐘都緊要，即刻去獸醫院。
title_en: Dog Gut Health: 5 Warning Signs Most Owners Miss
desc_en: About 70% of a dog's immune system lives in the gut. Learn the 5 warning signs of poor gut health — poop problems, bloating, itchy skin, low energy, and sudden grass-eating — and what to do about them.
content_html_en:
Short answer: About 70% of a dog's immune system lives in the gut — so gut problems often show up on the skin, in energy levels, and in the litter box before anything else. Here are the 5 signs most owners miss.

Why Gut Health Matters

Per Cornell Riney Canine Health Center, the gastrointestinal tract is a dog's largest immune organ — roughly 70% of immune cells live there. An unbalanced gut microbiome affects digestion, nutrient absorption, skin condition, and immunity.

The 5 Warning Signs

1. Poop Problems 💩

Persistent loose stools, constipation, or unusual colors (black, bloody, orange-yellow) are gut distress signals. One soft stool is no big deal — repeated or lasting episodes deserve attention.

2. Gas and Bloating 💨

Frequent gas may point to diet or microbiome imbalance. But a sudden hard, swollen belly with restlessness and unproductive retching could be GDV (bloat) — a life-threatening emergency. Go to a vet immediately.

3. Itchy Skin and Constant Scratching 🐾

Gut inflammation often shows on the skin — a weakened skin barrier means itching, redness, and recurring ear infections. If skin issues don't respond to topical treatment, look at the gut.

4. Low Energy ⚡

A struggling gut absorbs fewer nutrients. Chronic tiredness plus any other sign on this list is worth a gut health check.

5. Suddenly Eating Lots of Grass 🌱

Grass eating is usually normal — related to fiber or instinct; fewer than 25% of dogs vomit afterwards. A sudden increase, though, can signal gut discomfort worth discussing with your vet.

What You Can Do

  • Quality diet: stable, high-quality protein and fiber; avoid frequent food switches
  • Slow transitions: change foods over 7-10 days
  • Probiotics: vet-approved canine probiotics support microbiome balance
  • Regular deworming: parasites are a common gut culprit
  • Two or more signs? Book a gut health check with your vet

FAQ

Q: How long can diarrhea go on before seeing a vet?
Adult dogs: more than 24-48 hours, blood in stool, or lethargy/vomiting alongside — see a vet. Puppies: see a vet as soon as diarrhea starts.

Q: Is grass eating a gut problem?
Usually not — mostly instinct or fiber. A sudden increase deserves attention.

Q: When is a swollen belly an emergency?
Hard, swollen belly + restlessness + retching without vomiting = possible GDV. Every minute counts — go now.
disclaimer_en: For reference only. If your dog has persistent diarrhea, vomiting, or a hard swollen belly with restlessness, see a vet immediately.
source_en: Sources: Cornell Riney Canine Health Center, VCA Animal Hospitals, AAHA

title: 狗狗飲水多、尿多係咩事？5 個唔可以忽略嘅排尿變化
title_en: Dog Peeing More Often? 5 Urinary Changes You Should Never Ignore
desc_en: A sudden change in drinking or peeing is an early warning sign. Learn the five urinary changes to watch, the most common causes, and the red flags that need same-day care.
content_html:
一句話重點：狗狗飲水量或排尿習慣突然改變，通常唔係「老咗正常」——而係身體出咗事嘅早期訊號。最常見成因包括尿道感染、糖尿病、腎病同腎上腺疾病，全部要驗血驗尿先分得出。

點解要留意「飲水同排尿」？

腎臟係身體嘅過濾器。當腎臟、荷爾蒙系統或者泌尿道出問題，尿量會先變，然後飲水量跟住變（或反過來）。呢個連鎖反應令「飲水排尿」成為最容易在家觀察到嘅早期指標——但好多主人會等到狗狗明顯唔舒服先發現。

首先：正常係幾多？

犬隻正常飲水量大約係每日每公斤體重 40–60 毫升。即係一隻 25 公斤嘅狗，每日大約 1 至 1.5 公升。夏天、運動後、食乾糧嘅狗會飲多啲；但如果你發現水碗「填得比以前密」而狗狗生活習慣冇變，就值得量化記錄。

實用做法：用有刻度嘅水碗或量杯，連續量 3 日「24 小時飲水量 ÷ 體重」，帶住個數字去見獸醫，比講「好似飲多咗」有用好多。

五個唔可以忽略嘅排尿變化

  1. 飲多咗、尿多咗（同時出現）——獸醫叫 polydipsia（多飲）＋ polyuria（多尿）。多數情況係身體先排多咗尿，狗狗再飲水補返，所以兩樣通常一齊出現。
  2. 頻頻去廁所，但每次得幾滴——量少次多，通常指向下泌尿道問題（感染、結石、發炎），同「多尿」係兩件事。
  3. 屋企意外排尿、瞓覺漏尿——以前唔會，而家會；或者起身位置有尿漬。
  4. 尿味、尿色改變——特別深色／濃縮、帶血、或者阿摩尼亞味特別重。
  5. 維持排尿姿勢好耐、用力（straining）——呢個係紅旗，尤其配埋「尿唔出」。

最常見嘅成因

Cornell Riney Canine Health Center 列出嘅常見成因，可以分兩組：

A. 身體先排多尿 → 之後飲多水

  • 尿道／膀胱感染
  • 糖尿病（diabetes mellitus）
  • 腎臟疾病
  • 腎上腺疾病：庫欣氏症（Cushing's）或愛迪生氏症（Addison's）
  • 未絕育母犬嘅子宮蓄膿（pyometra）——可以係急症
  • 部分腫瘤（例如淋巴瘤）、肝病、鈎端螺旋體（leptospirosis）

B. 飲水本身係主因 → 之後尿多

  • 痛楚、壓力、天氣或環境太熱
  • 心因性多飲（psychogenic polydipsia）

兩組嘅處理方式完全唔同，所以唔可以靠觀察去「猜」——要驗血（CBC、生化）＋驗尿，獸醫亦可能會做尿比重、電解質等測試去收窄範圍。

幾時要即刻求醫（紅旗）

  • 用力但完全尿唔出——可能係尿道阻塞，屬緊急情況，拖延可以致命（公犬風險較高）。
  • 尿中帶血，或者尿味突然變得好臭。
  • 飲水量一兩日內突然倍增，或伴隨嘔吐、精神差、唔食嘢。
  • 未絕育母犬出現多飲多尿＋肚脹＋精神差——子宮蓄膿可以好急。

兩個常見錯誤

  1. 限制飲水——除咗獸醫明確指示（例如特定檢查前），自己收水會令脫水風險上升，對腎病狗尤其危險。
  2. 當「老咗係咁」——好多慢性腎病、糖尿病個案就係因為呢句而延誤。年齡唔係診斷。

你可以做嘅家居監測（3 樣）

  1. 連續 3 日量 24 小時飲水量，計 ml/kg。
  2. 記錄排尿：一日幾次、份量（多／少）、有冇用力、有冇意外。
  3. 影低尿色（自然光下），連記錄一齊交獸醫。

香港天氣注意

香港夏天又熱又濕，狗狗飲水量自然上升——所以「夏天飲多咗」係正常。判斷關鍵唔係單日數字，而係持續性：如果飲水量升咗之後冇回落，或者配埋上面任何一個紅旗，就唔應該再等。

參考文獻

  1. Cornell Richard P. Riney Canine Health Center — Canine Polyuria and Polydipsia (PU/PD), 2024.
  2. VCA Animal Hospitals — Testing for Increased Thirst and Urination.
  3. Polyuria and polydipsia: diagnostic approach and problems associated with patient evaluation. PubMed PMID 11570128.
content_html_en:
Short answer: a sudden change in how much your dog drinks or pees is rarely "just old age" — it is usually an early signal that something is wrong. The most common causes are urinary tract infection, diabetes, kidney disease and adrenal disease, and you cannot tell them apart without blood and urine tests.

Why drinking and peeing are the best early warning you have

The kidneys are the body's filter. When the kidneys, the hormone system or the urinary tract go wrong, urine volume usually changes first and water intake follows (or the other way round). That chain reaction makes drinking and peeing one of the few things you can measure at home — but most owners only notice once the dog is visibly unwell.

First, what is normal?

A healthy dog usually drinks about 40–60 ml per kilogram of body weight per day. For a 25 kg dog that is roughly 1 to 1.5 litres a day. Hot weather, exercise and dry food all push intake up. The signal to watch is a change from your dog's own baseline.

Practical method: use a measuring jug or a graduated bowl and record 24-hour intake for three days, then divide by body weight. A number your vet can compare beats "he seems to drink more".

Five urinary changes you should never ignore

  1. Drinking more and peeing more, together — polydipsia plus polyuria. In most cases the body loses more water in urine first and the dog drinks to replace it, so the two appear together.
  2. Going out often but passing only a few drops — small volume, high frequency points to lower urinary tract problems (infection, stones, inflammation), which is a different problem from polyuria.
  3. Accidents indoors or leaking while asleep — especially in a dog that never used to.
  4. A change in colour or smell — very dark or concentrated urine, blood-tinged urine, or a strong ammonia smell.
  5. Straining, or holding the position for a long time — a red flag, particularly together with little or no urine coming out.

The most common causes

Cornell's Riney Canine Health Center groups the common causes into two patterns:

A. The body passes more urine → the dog drinks more

  • Urinary tract infection
  • Diabetes mellitus
  • Kidney disease
  • Adrenal gland disease — Cushing's syndrome or Addison's disease
  • Pyometra (uterine infection) in unspayed females — can become an emergency
  • Certain cancers (e.g. lymphoma), liver disease, leptospirosis

B. Drinking is the primary problem → urine follows

  • Pain, stress, heat (room or outdoor temperature)
  • Psychogenic polydipsia

These two patterns are managed completely differently, which is why you cannot diagnose by watching. Screening usually means a complete blood count, a serum biochemistry profile and a urinalysis, with follow-up tests such as urine specific gravity or electrolytes to narrow it down.

When to seek help the same day

  • Straining with no urine coming out — a possible urethral obstruction; this is an emergency and can be fatal if left (higher risk in male dogs).
  • Blood in the urine, or a sudden strong smell.
  • Water intake doubling within a day or two, especially with vomiting, lethargy or going off food.
  • An unspayed female with increased drinking and urination, a bloated abdomen and lethargy — pyometra can progress quickly.

Two mistakes owners make

  1. Restricting water — unless a vet has specifically asked you to (for example before a particular test), withholding water risks dehydration and is especially dangerous in kidney disease.
  2. Blaming age — "he's just getting older" is how a lot of chronic kidney disease and diabetes gets diagnosed late. Age is not a diagnosis.

Three things you can track at home

  1. Measure 24-hour water intake for three days and work out ml/kg.
  2. Log urination: how often, how much (a lot / a few drops), any straining, any accidents.
  3. Photograph urine colour in natural light and take the log with you.

A note for Hong Kong owners

Hong Kong summers are hot and humid, so intake naturally rises — that part is normal. What matters is persistence: if intake goes up and does not come back down, or any red flag above appears alongside it, do not wait it out.

Sources

  1. Cornell Richard P. Riney Canine Health Center — Canine Polyuria and Polydipsia (PU/PD), 2024.
  2. VCA Animal Hospitals — Testing for Increased Thirst and Urination.
  3. Polyuria and polydipsia: diagnostic approach and problems associated with patient evaluation. PubMed PMID 11570128.
source: 參考：Cornell Riney Canine Health Center、VCA Animal Hospitals、PubMed 11570128
source_en: Sources: Cornell Riney Canine Health Center; VCA Animal Hospitals; PubMed 11570128
disclaimer: 本文僅供參考，不能代替獸醫診斷。狗狗完全尿唔出、用力排尿、尿中帶血或精神突然變差，請即日求醫。
disclaimer_en: For reference only — this does not replace veterinary diagnosis. If your dog cannot pass urine, is straining, has blood in the urine or suddenly deteriorates, seek veterinary care the same day.

title: 狗狗夜晚咳？3 個同心臟有關嘅警號
title_en: Dog Coughing at Night? 3 Heart-Related Warning Signs
desc_en: Night-time coughing in dogs often points to left-sided heart failure or tracheal collapse. Learn the three warning signs, how to measure sleeping breathing rate, and when it is urgent.
content_html:
一句話重點：狗狗夜晚或者休息時咳，唔一定係「喉嚨敏感」。兩個最常見嘅方向係左側心臟衰竭（肺積水）同氣管塌陷——兩者要靠 X 光／超聲波分辨，唔可以靠咳聲估。

點解夜晚特別容易咳？

當狗狗躺低，身體姿勢改變，肺部血液同液體分布會唔同；如果心臟泵血能力下降，液體會滲入肺組織（肺積水 / pulmonary edema），刺激氣道引起咳同呼吸吃力。呢個就係左側心臟衰竭嘅典型機制——而左側心臟衰竭係最常見嘅心臟衰竭類型。

另一邊，氣管塌陷（tracheal collapse）嘅咳亦特別容易喺夜晚、興奮、又熱又濕嘅天氣、食完飲完之後加劇（頸圈壓住氣管都會）。

三個要留意嘅警號

  1. 夜晚／休息時持續咳，運動後加劇——唔係偶爾咳一兩聲，而係每晚都出現，或者一散步就咳。
  2. 休息時呼吸次數上升——瞓覺或者靜止時呼吸率係最實用嘅家居指標。研究顯示亞臨床心臟病嘅狗狗瞓覺呼吸率平均低於每分鐘 30 次；如果持續偏高，就係要檢查嘅訊號。
  3. 耐力下降、容易累、甚至暈倒——唔願行、行兩步就喘、突然腳軟；如果牙肉或舌頭發紫，屬急症。

家居可以量嘅一個數字：睡覺呼吸率

狗狗熟睡時，睇住胸腹起伏，數 30 秒再乘 2，就係每分鐘呼吸次數。每日喺同一時間（例如剛入睡）量一次，記錄成趨勢。重點唔係單日數字，而係幾日之間係唔係越嚟越高。帶住記錄去見獸醫，比「好似喘咗」有用好多。

咳嗽仲有咩其他常見原因？

  • 氣管塌陷——乾、硬、「鵝鳴」式咳；多見於中年至老年（約 4–14 歲）小型犬，但任何體型都可能發生。
  • 呼吸道感染（例如犬舍咳）——通常伴隨其他狗狗接觸史。
  • 心絲蟲、慢性支氣管炎、喉部問題——要獸醫檢查分辨。

呢個清單嘅意思係：夜晚咳係一個徵狀，唔係一個診斷。

幾時要即刻求醫

  • 呼吸困難：明顯用力呼吸、腹部大力起伏、唔肯躺低。
  • 牙肉或舌頭發紫（缺氧）、暈倒。
  • 腹部脹大、精神突然變差。
  • 休息呼吸率持續偏高（連續幾日明顯升）——唔好等。

兩個常見錯誤

  1. 當係「食得太快／反胃」——如果每晚都有，性質就唔同。
  2. 自己俾人用止咳藥——好多人用藥物對狗有毒，而且止咳會遮蓋病情。

參考文獻

  1. VCA Animal Hospitals — Congestive Heart Failure in Dogs.
  2. VCA Animal Hospitals — Tracheal Collapse in Dogs.
  3. Sleeping and resting respiratory rates in dogs and cats with medically-controlled left-sided congestive heart failure. Vet J 2016. PubMed PMID 26639825.
content_html_en:
Short answer: a dog coughing at night or at rest is not automatically "just a sensitive throat". The two most common directions are left-sided heart failure (fluid in the lungs) and tracheal collapse, and you cannot tell them apart from the sound of the cough — that needs imaging.

Why night-time coughing matters

When a dog lies down, the distribution of blood and fluid in the chest changes. If the heart cannot pump efficiently, fluid seeps into the lung tissue (pulmonary edema), which irritates the airways and causes coughing and laboured breathing. This is the classic mechanism of left-sided congestive heart failure — the most common form of heart failure in dogs.

Tracheal collapse behaves differently but also peaks at night: the cough is typically worse at night, with excitement, in hot or humid weather, immediately after eating or drinking, and when pressure is applied to the trachea (for example by a collar).

Three warning signs to watch

  1. Coughing at night or at rest, and worse with exercise — not an occasional cough, but something that happens most nights or every walk.
  2. A rising resting breathing rate — sleeping respiratory rate is the most practical home metric. Research shows dogs with subclinical heart disease average below 30 breaths per minute while asleep; a persistent rise above that is a reason to get checked.
  3. Reduced exercise tolerance, tiring quickly, fainting — stopping on walks, lagging behind, sudden weakness. Blue gums or tongue is an emergency.

One number you can measure at home

While your dog is sound asleep, count chest or belly movements for 30 seconds and double it. Record it once a day at the same moment (for example soon after falling asleep). What matters is the trend over several days, not a single reading — and a written log is far more useful to your vet than "he seems to breathe harder".

Other common causes of coughing

  • Tracheal collapse — a persistent, dry, harsh "goose honk" cough; most frequent in middle-aged to senior dogs (roughly 4–14 years) and in small breeds, though any size can be affected.
  • Respiratory infection (e.g. kennel cough) — usually with a history of contact with other dogs.
  • Heartworm, chronic bronchitis, laryngeal disease — these need veterinary assessment to separate.

The point of that list: night coughing is a symptom, not a diagnosis.

When to seek care urgently

  • Difficulty breathing — obvious effort, strong abdominal movement, unwilling to lie down.
  • Blue gums or tongue (lack of oxygen), fainting.
  • A bloated abdomen or a sudden drop in energy.
  • A resting breathing rate that stays elevated for several days — do not wait it out.

Two mistakes owners make

  1. Blaming it on eating too fast or reflux — if it happens every night, the pattern is different.
  2. Giving human cough medicine — many human medicines are toxic to dogs, and suppressing the cough hides the disease.

Sources

  1. VCA Animal Hospitals — Congestive Heart Failure in Dogs.
  2. VCA Animal Hospitals — Tracheal Collapse in Dogs.
  3. Sleeping and resting respiratory rates in dogs and cats with medically-controlled left-sided congestive heart failure. Vet J 2016. PubMed PMID 26639825.

disclaimer: 本文僅供參考，不能代替獸醫診斷。狗狗出現呼吸困難、牙肉發紫或暈倒，請即時求醫。
disclaimer_en: For reference only — this does not replace veterinary diagnosis. If your dog has difficulty breathing, blue gums or faints, seek emergency care immediately.

title: 狗狗膀胱感染（尿道炎）徵狀同檢查流程
title_en: Bladder Infection in Dogs: Signs, Tests and Why Culture Matters
desc_en: Frequent urination, straining and blood in the urine are the classic signs of a bladder infection in dogs — but stones look the same. Here are the tests that matter and the red flags.
content_html:
一句話重點：頻尿、用力、血尿、突然喺屋企尿——典型下泌尿道感染徵狀。但膀胱結石、腫瘤等情況嘅表現一模一樣，所以要驗尿＋種菌（culture），唔係「驗到有菌就食抗生素」。

最常見嘅六個徵狀

  1. 排尿時用力（straining）
  2. 頻頻去，但每次得少量
  3. 屋企意外排尿（以前唔會）
  4. 尿味特別臭
  5. 成日舔生殖部位
  6. 尿中帶血

感染通常係細菌由尿道走入膀胱引起；膀胱內嘅尿本來無菌，但細菌一入去就可以繁殖。最常見嘅細菌係大腸桿菌（E. coli），亦有機會同時有多過一種菌。

邊啲狗狗風險較高？

本身有呢啲情況嘅狗狗會較易有尿道感染：膀胱結石、尿失禁／糞便失禁、糖尿病、庫欣氏症（Cushing's）、腎病、腫瘤。呢個就係點解「成日復發」通常唔係因為運氣差，而係背後有個未處理嘅原因。

獸醫會做嘅檢查（同點解）

  1. 驗尿（urinalysis）——睇白血球、細菌、紅血球、酸鹼值同尿比重。有幾種泌尿問題會「扮」感染，所以呢步一定要做。
  2. 膀胱穿刺抽尿（cystocentesis）——用針由膀胱直接抽尿，避免收集過程嘅外部污染（自由接尿容易混入環境細菌）。
  3. 種菌＋藥敏測試（culture & sensitivity）——確認係邊種菌、對邊種抗生素有效。國際指引（ISCAID）強調準確診斷＋針對性用藥，因為胡亂用抗生素會造成抗藥性。
  4. 影像檢查——如果懷疑結石，獸醫可能安排 X 光或超聲波。

「復發」點定義？

一般定義係 6 個月內兩次，或者一年內三次以上。呢種情況通常要進一步查根本原因（結石、結構問題、內分泌病），而唔係再食一輪抗生素就算。

紅旗：即日求醫

  • 用力但完全尿唔出——可能係尿道阻塞，屬急症（公犬風險較高），可以致命。
  • 尿中帶血塊，或者精神差、嘔吐、唔食嘢。
  • 未絕育母犬出現多飲多尿＋肚脹——要排除子宮蓄膿。

家居上你可以做嘅事

  1. 確保飲水充足：多放水碗或使用飲水機，並勤清洗（香港潮濕，水碗容易成為細菌溫床）。
  2. 記錄排尿頻率、份量、有冇用力、有冇血——帶住記錄去見獸醫。
  3. 唔好自己停藥或者重用上次剩低嘅抗生素——徵狀好轉唔等於細菌清乾淨。

參考文獻

  1. Cornell Richard P. Riney Canine Health Center — Urinary Tract Infections in Dogs.
  2. VCA Animal Hospitals — Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs) in Dogs.
  3. ISCAID guidelines for the diagnosis and management of bacterial urinary tract infections in dogs and cats. Vet J 2019. PubMed PMID 30971357.
  4. Antimicrobial Resistance in Companion Animals: 30-month analysis of urinary tract infection isolates. Animals 2025. PubMed PMID 40509013.
content_html_en:
Short answer: going out constantly, straining, blood in the urine and sudden accidents indoors are the classic signs of a lower urinary tract infection. But bladder stones and other conditions look identical — which is why testing (and a urine culture) matters more than "there are bacteria, so let's use antibiotics".

The six most common signs

  1. Straining to urinate
  2. Frequent trips passing only small amounts
  3. Accidents in the house in a previously reliable dog
  4. Unusually foul-smelling urine
  5. Excessive licking of the genital area
  6. Blood in the urine

Infection usually happens when bacteria travel up the urethra into the bladder. Urine inside the bladder is normally sterile, but once bacteria arrive they can multiply. The most common organism is E. coli, and sometimes more than one type of bacteria is involved.

Which dogs are at higher risk?

Dogs with any of the following are more susceptible: bladder stones, urinary or fecal incontinence, diabetes, Cushing's disease, kidney disease, or cancer. That is why repeated infections are usually not bad luck — there is often an underlying condition that has not been addressed.

What the tests are for

  1. Urinalysis — white blood cells, bacteria, red blood cells, pH and urine specific gravity. Several urinary disorders mimic infection, so this step matters.
  2. Cystocentesis — a needle collects urine directly from the bladder, avoiding contamination from the environment (free-catch samples pick up environmental bacteria).
  3. Urine culture and sensitivity — identifies which bacteria are present and which antibiotic actually works. The international ISCAID guidelines stress accurate diagnosis and targeted treatment, because inappropriate antibiotic use drives resistance.
  4. Imaging — if stones are suspected, X-rays or ultrasound may be recommended.

What counts as "recurrent"?

Recurrent infection is generally defined as two infections within six months, or three within a year. That pattern calls for a search for the underlying cause — stones, structural problems, endocrine disease — rather than another round of antibiotics alone.

Red flags: seek care the same day

  • Straining with no urine coming out — possible urethral obstruction, an emergency (higher risk in male dogs) that can be fatal.
  • Blood clots in the urine, or vomiting, lethargy and going off food.
  • An unspayed female with increased drinking and urination plus a bloated abdomen — pyometra must be ruled out.

What you can do at home

  1. Keep water available and fresh: multiple bowls or a fountain, cleaned often — in Hong Kong's humidity a dirty bowl is a bacterial reservoir.
  2. Log urination frequency, volume, straining and any blood, and take the log with you.
  3. Never stop treatment early or reuse leftover antibiotics — symptoms improving does not mean the bacteria are gone.

Sources

  1. Cornell Richard P. Riney Canine Health Center — Urinary Tract Infections in Dogs.
  2. VCA Animal Hospitals — Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs) in Dogs.
  3. ISCAID guidelines for the diagnosis and management of bacterial urinary tract infections in dogs and cats. Vet J 2019. PubMed PMID 30971357.
  4. Antimicrobial Resistance in Companion Animals: 30-month analysis of urinary tract infection isolates. Animals 2025. PubMed PMID 40509013.

title: 狗狗皮膚痕癢？「邊度痕」已經透露咗原因
title_en: Dog Itchy Skin? Where Your Dog Itches Already Narrows Down the Cause
desc_en: Dog itchy skin: use where your dog itches to narrow down the cause, run a 5-step home check, and know what actually helps and when to see a vet.
content_html:
一句話重點：狗皮膚痕癢係徵狀，唔係診斷。最快嘅線索係痕邊度：尾根同背脊中後段指向跳蚤，腳掌／面／耳／腋下／腹部指向環境或食物過敏，只有耳仔有事多數係耳道發炎。

痕癢係一個「循環」，唔係一個病

痕癢（pruritus）係「皮膚上一種令人想抓嘅不適感」。最常見嘅三大方向係寄生蟲、感染、過敏。

越抓越痕係一個循環：皮膚屏障受損 → 發炎同痕癢 → 抓、舔、磨 → 皮膚再破損 → 細菌或酵母感染 → 更加痕。循環一旦形成，就算最初嘅原因已經過去，痕癢一樣可以繼續。

第一步：睇「邊度痕」，位置已經係線索

痕癢位置最可能嘅方向
尾根、背脊中後段、大腿後側跳蚤過敏性皮膚炎（一歲以下好少見，多數喺晚夏）
腳掌、面、耳殼、前腳摺位、腋下、腹部環境過敏或食物過敏（通常 6 個月至 3 歲開始）
只有耳仔：搖頭、臭味、分泌物外耳炎（過敏狗最多五成有，可能係唯一徵狀）

位置係方向唔係診斷——好多狗同時有兩三樣問題，先處理寄生蟲同感染係必要嘅一步。

5 步家居檢查

  1. 跳蚤梳加白紙測試——梳尾根同背脊中後段，黑色粒粒放喺濕白紙巾上溶開變紅褐色就係跳蚤糞便。極度敏感嘅狗會舔到幾乎冇跳蚤，搵唔到唔等於冇跳蚤過敏。
  2. 睇皮膚——紅、腫、傷口、脫毛、口水染色（毛變紅褐）、皮膚變厚變黑。
  3. 檢查耳仔——有冇臭味同分泌物；深色分泌物常見於酵母或寄生蟲。
  4. 對時間線——每年同一時段發作似花粉、黴菌；全年痕更似塵蟎同／或食物過敏。最近換過糧、零食、洗毛液？
  5. 寫低開始日期同頻率——幾時開始、日夜有冇分別、有冇影響睡眠。

常見成因（同香港氣候嘅關係）

  • 寄生蟲：跳蚤同跳蚤過敏（徵狀多見於腹部下方同腹股溝）、蟎蟲、蝨——獸醫第一樣要排除。
  • 環境致敏原：塵蟎、花粉、黴菌。香港又熱又濕，塵蟎喺潮濕位置同布藝傢俬、床褥特別多，環境過敏好多時全年都會痕。
  • 食物過敏：要靠飲食試驗確認；血液或皮膚測試驗唔到食物過敏。
  • 二次感染同皮膚乾：酵母（Malassezia）、葡萄球菌感染會令痕癢加劇；皮膚水分同 pH 隨年齡品種改變。

真正幫到手嘅做法，同唔好做嘅事

  • 全年定時用獸醫建議嘅寄生蟲預防，唔止夏天。
  • 床品每星期 60°C 水洗，用可抹洗嘅床；塵蟎敏感嘅狗減少地毯、唔好上床、保持屋企乾爽。
  • 散步後抹身抹腳，腳趾縫要抹乾，減少黏喺毛上嘅花粉。
  • 用獸醫建議嘅藥性或屏障支援洗毛液；唔好用人類洗頭水——狗皮膚 pH 中位數約 6.1–6.6，比人類皮膚表面嘅酸性（約 pH 4.5–5.5）鹼。
  • 唔好自己俾人類抗組織胺：獸醫文獻指出抗組織胺止狗痕效果差異極大，研究唔支持用嚟止痕；亦唔好用人類類固醇藥膏、精油或白醋搽上痕嘅皮膚。

如果懷疑食物過敏：飲食試驗要幾長？

過敏指引建議做 4–12 星期，並喺第 2–3 星期開始停止痕藥評估反應；皮膚問題一般要至少 8 星期（部分狗 30 日已有反應，但唔可以就此判定）。期間只可以食獸醫指定嘅飲食，零食同咬膠都要跟同一規則。

幾時要睇獸醫

  • 皮膚已抓破、流膿、有明顯傷口或熱點（hot spot）。
  • 脫毛範圍擴大、皮膚變厚變黑；耳仔有臭味、分泌物、摸親都痛。
  • 痕癢影響睡眠、食慾或情緒；或者每日抓、舔超過 4–5 次。
  • 家居步驟做足兩星期都冇改善，或者突然劇烈痕癢——大部分過敏皮膚問題可以控制，但唔一定斷尾。
content_html_en:
Short answer: itchy skin is a symptom, not a diagnosis. Where the dog itches is the first clue: tail base and lower back = fleas; paws, face, ears, armpits and belly = environmental or food allergy; ears alone = ear canal infection.

The itch-scratch cycle, in plain terms

Pruritus is a skin sensation that provokes scratching — a sign, not a disease. Usual directions: parasites, infections, allergies.

Itching loops: barrier damage → inflammation and itch → scratching and licking → broken skin → infection → more itch. So the trigger may be long gone while the itch continues.

Step one: where the dog itches is already a clue

  • Tail base, lower back, back of thighs — flea allergy dermatitis (rare under one year; mostly late summer).
  • Paws, face, ear flaps, armpits, belly — environmental or food allergy (onset usually 6 months–3 years).
  • Ears only: head shaking, smell, discharge — otitis externa; up to half of allergic dogs get it, sometimes as the only sign.

A direction, not a diagnosis: many dogs have two or three problems at once.

A 5-step home check

  1. Flea comb plus damp-paper test — comb the tail base and lower back, then put the black specks on damp towel. Flea dirt is reddish black and dissolves into a reddish brown stain. Sensitive dogs can look flea-free, so finding nothing proves nothing.
  2. Check the skin — redness, swelling, sores, bald patches, brown saliva stains, thickened or darkened skin.
  3. Check the ears — smell or discharge? Dark discharge often means yeast or parasites.
  4. Plot a timeline — same season yearly = pollen or mould; year-round itch = dust mites and/or food allergy.
  5. Log onset and frequency — when it started, day versus night, disturbed sleep.

Common causes, and why Hong Kong matters

  • Parasites: fleas (signs often on the abdomen and groin), mites, lice — the first thing a vet rules out.
  • Environmental allergens: dust mites, pollens, moulds. Humidity lets dust mites thrive in damp rooms and bedding, so this is often year-round.
  • Food allergy: found by a diet trial; blood and skin tests cannot detect it.
  • Secondary infection and dry skin: yeast (Malassezia) and Staphylococcus infections are common and worsen itch.

What helps, and what to avoid

  • Year-round parasite prevention as your vet advises, not just in summer.
  • Wash bedding weekly at 60°C; for dust-mite sensitive dogs cut carpets, keep the dog off sofas and beds, and dehumidify.
  • Wipe the coat and paws after walks and dry between the toes to remove pollen.
  • Use a vet-recommended medicated or barrier-supporting shampoo, never a human shampoo: median dog skin pH is about 6.1–6.6 versus roughly pH 4.5–5.5 on human skin.
  • No human antihistamines — current research does not support them for itch relief in dogs. No human steroid creams, oils or vinegar either.

If food allergy is suspected: how long is a diet trial?

Guidelines recommend 4–12 weeks, with anti-itch medication stopped at week 2–3 to judge the response. Skin cases usually need at least 8 weeks; some respond within 30 days, but that alone is not conclusive. Only the prescribed diet is allowed.

When to see a vet

  • Skin is broken or weeping, or there is an obvious sore or hot spot.
  • Hair loss is spreading, skin thickening or darkening, or an ear smells or discharges.
  • Itching disturbs sleep, appetite or mood, or the dog scratches or licks over 4–5 times a day.
  • Two weeks of home steps bring no improvement, or itching starts suddenly and severely. Most allergy-related skin disease is controlled, not cured.
source: 參考：Merck Veterinary Manual（Itching/Pruritus in Dogs、Fleas of Dogs、Atopic Dermatitis in Dogs、Ear Infections and Otitis Externa in Dogs）、VCA Animal Hospitals（Pruritus: Itching and Scratching in Dogs）、AAHA 2023 Management of Allergic Diseases in Dogs and Cats Guidelines、University of Nottingham Itchy Dog Project、PDSA（Itchy skin in dogs）、PMC12420860、PMC11096370、Tufts University Petfoodology

disclaimer: 本文僅供參考，不能代替獸醫診斷。皮膚痕癢嘅原因要由獸醫檢查分辨；唔好自己俾狗用人類藥物或類固醇藥膏。如果皮膚已破損、有臭味分泌物，或者痕癢影響睡眠，請盡快求醫。
disclaimer_en: For reference only — this does not replace veterinary diagnosis. The cause of itchy skin has to be worked out by a vet; never give your dog human medicines or steroid creams. See a vet promptly if the skin is broken, there is smelly discharge, or itching is disturbing sleep.

title: 狗狗跛行係關節痛定拉傷？前腳／後腳跛行嘅判別同紅旗
title_en: Dog Limping: Strain or Joint Pain? How to Tell Front-Leg and Back-Leg Lameness Apart
desc_en: Dog limping on a front or back leg? Learn how to tell a soft-tissue strain from joint pain, the after-rest stiffness pattern that points to arthritis, the signs owners miss, and the red flags that mean emergency.
content_html:
一句話重點：狗狗跛行係一個徵狀，唔係一個病——拉傷、關節退化、韌帶斷裂甚至神經問題都可以令狗跛。分辨關鍵唔係「跛得幾嚴重」，而係模式：幾時跛、跛邊隻腳、休息後係好轉定變差。

第一步：拉傷，定係關節問題？

急劇出現嘅跛行，最常見原因係斷趾甲、軟組織拉傷或扭傷、關節受傷、骨折同關節脫位；慢性或反覆出現嘅跛行，通常同骨關節炎、脊椎變形、神經問題或腫瘤有關。急性拉傷靠限制活動同止痛；關節問題就要長期管理——先睇時間線，唔係先估嚴重程度。

關節痛嘅經典模式：起身最僵，行一陣又順返

骨關節炎（osteoarthritis, OA）嘅典型表現唔係「一路跛」，而係僵硬，休息之後最明顯。PDSA 就係咁形容：僵硬「特別係休息後或者散步後」出現。好多狗主形容，狗狗起身後最初幾分鐘最僵，行順咗之後好似回復正常，所以好易當成「老咗姐」。（時間長短屬狗主常見描述，唔係研究數據。）

但 OA 唔係「老就一定有」——VCA 明確指出單純老化並唔係 OA 成因，體重、關節結構（如髖／肘關節發育不良）同舊傷都有關。至少 20% 一歲以上嘅狗、80% 八歲以上嘅狗有 OA。

唔一定見到跛：容易漏嘅信號

好多關節痛嘅狗唔會明顯跛，只係「慢咗、靜咗」。PDSA 提醒：狗好叻忍痛。

  • 起身、趴低變慢，要試幾次才起到身
  • 唔願意跳上梳化／上車，開始避樓梯
  • 行得慢、行喺你旁邊或後面，背脊微拱，後腳肌肉變薄
  • 精神變差、易嬲、瞓多咗，關節腫大或附近毛髮被口水染黃

前後腳有分別：前腳痛嘅狗，患腳承重時通常抬高頭；後腳痛嘅狗則低頭（Merck Veterinary Manual 描述嘅頭部擺動現象）。「坐得唔正」（後腳歪埋一邊）要考慮十字韌帶疾病——完全斷裂時可突然好跛、唔敢承重；肥胖係風險因素。

拖腳係另一回事：後腳腳背反轉落地（knuckling）或腳背刮地刮到脫毛，係神經問題（如退化性脊髓病）嘅表現，唔係關節痛。

舔／咬同一隻腳：痛，定係皮膚問題？

PDSA 指出，成日舔同一個位（over-grooming）可能係痛嘅表現。但舔腳亦可以係趾間異物（玻璃碎、草籽）、趾甲裂、趾墊傷口或趾間感染。可以由趾間、趾墊、趾甲逐一檢查；狗明顯痛就唔好夾硬㩒。

紅旗：以下情況唔可以等

  • 完全唔肯承重、企唔穩或行唔到——骨折、韌帶全斷或關節脫位嘅狗一般唔會行得正常
  • 突然發生而且有明顯創傷（被車撞、被大狗咬起搖、跳落樓梯）
  • 拖腳、腳背反轉落地，或者摸頸／摸背就痛
  • 急性痛或跛行超過一個鐘未好轉
  • 跛之餘唔肯食超過 12 小時，或精神明顯轉差
  • 跛行超過 24 小時就應該睇獸醫——拖越久越難醫，狗亦會用其他腳代償，引發第二個問題

獸醫會做咩？

  1. 睇步態（休息、起身、行路）＋骨關節檢查：摸骨同關節，睇腫脹、痛點、不穩定同肌肉萎縮。
  2. X 光睇骨折、關節變化（發炎或 OA）、軟組織腫脹同腫瘤，影得準可能要鎮靜；有需要會抽關節液化驗或驗血。
  3. 有時會先用消炎止痛藥加限制活動做「診斷性治療」再覆診——跛行好多時要靠時間線才睇得出。

家居可以做嘅 5 件事

  1. 控制體重：有實驗數據支持。一篇 16 星期減重研究（PMC2855019）發現，肥胖同時有 OA 嘅狗，體重減 6.10% 後跛行評分已顯著改善；減 8.85% 後儀器步態分析亦支持改善。
  2. 舖防滑：關節痛嘅狗肌肉較弱、易滑倒，一滑就可能再受傷。用地墊或防滑墊蓋住佢最常用嘅路線（香港多硬地磚，呢點特別重要）。
  3. 斜台或腳踏：上車、上下梳化用斜台，減少跳躍。
  4. 控制式散步：每日短而規律，避免突然加量；唔好跳、唔好急停滑行、唔好追波、唔好行崎嶇地面。
  5. 環境微調：軟墊床、食水兜升至肘部高度、關節保暖（暖水袋要包毛巾，唔可留狗自己一個）。躺太耐會更僵，鼓勵佢間中起身郁下。

關節保健品：證據要點睇？

獸醫常用葡萄糖胺（glucosamine）同軟骨素（chondroitin），但一篇同行評審回顧（PMC5356289）直接寫：即使「證據有限而且互相矛盾」，呢兩隻產品仍然被普遍推薦，並指現時缺乏設計良好嘅臨床研究確認真正療效。VCA 亦建議要問獸醫有咩科學數據支持；PDSA 亦講明保健品「唔可以代替藥物，而且唔係隻隻狗有效」。另外唔好俾人用藥——好多人用止痛藥對狗有毒，而且會遮蓋病情。結論：保健品可以當輔助，唔應該代替獸醫處方嘅治療。

Short answer: a limp is a symptom, not a diagnosis. Strains, worn joints, torn ligaments and nerve problems all look alike from the sofa — the pattern is what separates them: when it started, which leg, and whether rest makes it better or worse.

Step one: strain, or joint problem?

Sudden lameness is most often a broken nail, soft-tissue strain or sprain, joint injury, fracture or dislocation. Chronic or on-and-off limping usually means osteoarthritis, spinal or limb deformity, a neurologic disorder or cancer. A strain needs rest and pain relief; joint disease needs long-term management. Read the timeline before judging severity.

The arthritis pattern: stiff after rest, looser with movement

Osteoarthritis (OA) rarely shows up as non-stop limping. It shows up as stiffness, worst after rest — PDSA calls it stiffness "especially after rest or after walks". Owners often say the first few minutes after getting up are worst, the dog looking nearly normal once it moves. That is why it gets dismissed as "just getting old". (The time window is an owner observation, not a research figure.)

OA is not inevitable with age: VCA states ageing alone is not a cause — weight, joint structure (hip or elbow dysplasia) and past injuries matter. At least 20% of dogs over one year old, and 80% over eight, have OA.

You may never see an obvious limp

Most dogs with sore joints never limp obviously. They get slower and quieter — as PDSA puts it, dogs are very good at hiding pain.

  • Slow to get up or lie down, sometimes needing a couple of tries
  • Reluctance to jump onto the sofa or into the car, or avoiding stairs
  • Walking slowly, beside or behind you, with a slightly hunched spine or thinning hind-leg muscle
  • Lower energy, grumpiness, sleeping more, swollen joints or saliva-stained fur around a joint

Front and back legs look different. A sore forelimb makes a dog raise its head as that leg takes weight; a sore hindlimb makes it drop its head — the head-nod pattern in the Merck Veterinary Manual. Sitting off to one side (a "lazy sit") points to possible cruciate ligament disease, which can rupture suddenly. Excess weight is a risk factor.

Dragging is different. A hind paw that knuckles over or scrapes the ground until the top loses hair suggests a neurologic problem such as degenerative myelopathy, not joint pain.

Licking or chewing one paw: pain, or skin?

PDSA notes that over-grooming — licking one spot far more than usual — can signal pain. Paw licking also has ordinary causes: a foreign body between the toes (glass, grass seed), a split nail, a cut pad or infection between the toes. Check each toe space, pad and nail; if your dog is sore, do not force it.

Red flags: do not wait these out

  • Complete refusal to bear weight, or unable to stand and walk without help — fractures, torn ligaments and dislocations usually stop a dog walking normally
  • Sudden onset after obvious trauma (hit by a car, shaken by a larger dog, a fall down stairs)
  • Dragging or knuckling a paw, or pain when the neck or back is touched
  • Acute pain or limping not settled within an hour
  • Limping plus refusing food for over 12 hours, or a clear drop in energy
  • Limping beyond 24 hours should be seen by a vet — waiting makes it harder to treat, and dogs compensate with the other legs, creating a second problem

What your vet will do

  1. Watch the gait (at rest, getting up, walking) and run an orthopaedic exam — feeling bones and joints for swelling, pain, instability and muscle wasting.
  2. X-rays for fractures, joint change (inflammation or OA), soft-tissue swelling and tumours, often under sedation; further tests may include joint fluid analysis or bloodwork.
  3. Sometimes a trial of anti-inflammatories plus restricted exercise acts as a diagnostic step, with a recheck after — lameness often only declares itself over time.

Five things you can do at home

  1. Control body weight. This has trial data behind it: in a 16-week weight-loss study (PMC2855019), obese dogs with OA scored significantly better on lameness after losing 6.10% of body weight, with gait analysis supporting improvement from 8.85%.
  2. Fix the flooring. Arthritic dogs have weaker muscles and slip easily, and a slip can cause a fresh injury. Rugs or non-slip mats on the routes your dog uses most — relevant in Hong Kong flats, which are mostly hard tile.
  3. Use a ramp or step for the car and sofa so your dog jumps less.
  4. Controlled leash walks. Short and regular, no sudden increases, no jumping or skidding, no ball chasing, no rough ground.
  5. Adjust the environment. Padded bedding, bowls raised to elbow height, warmth for sore joints (wrap a hot water bottle in a towel; never leave it with the dog alone). Lying still for hours stiffens joints, so encourage movement during the day.

Joint supplements: what does the evidence say?

Vets commonly recommend glucosamine and chondroitin, and a peer-reviewed review (PMC5356289) says so plainly: despite "limited and conflicting evidence", these products remain widely used, with a shortage of well-designed clinical studies confirming real benefit. VCA points the same way — ask your vet what scientific data supports the product; PDSA adds that supplements are no replacement for medication and do not work for every dog. So treat them as support, not a substitute for prescribed treatment. And never reach for human painkillers: many are toxic to dogs and they hide the disease while it progresses.

title: 狗狗蜱蟲跳蚤全攻略：香港全年風險、拔蜱唔好做嘅事
title_en: Dog Ticks and Fleas in Hong Kong: Year-Round Risk and How to Remove a Tick Safely
desc_en: Fleas vs ticks in Hong Kong dogs: why ticks matter more, the tick-borne diseases seen locally (babesiosis, ehrlichiosis, anaplasmosis, spotted fever), how to do a full-body tick check, correct tick removal, and why year-round flea and tick prevention is needed in a subtropical climate.
content_html:
一句話重點：蚤同蜱係兩種問題——蚤令狗狗痕、搞皮膚，蜱會傳病（香港最常見係巴貝斯蟲「蜱熱」）。香港氣候濕暖，兩者都唔係夏天限定；散步後兩分鐘嘅全身檢查，係最有效嘅一步。

蜱同蚤有咩分別？

蜱屬蛛形綱，成蜱八隻腳；蚤係無翼昆蟲，六隻腳。蚤咬會痕、可引起蚤過敏性皮膚炎，嚴重感染（尤其幼犬）可因失血貧血，亦傳播絛蟲。蜱咬住唔放、幾日都唔覺，而且會傳播多種病原：巴貝斯蟲、埃里希體（Ehrlichia）、無形體（Anaplasma）、立克次體——所以蜱更值得緊張。硬蜱一生更有超過九成時間唔在宿主身上，係躲喺草叢等動物經過。（VCA；Merck）

香港情況：點解要全年防？

香港屬亞熱帶季風氣候，環境有利媒介繁殖（Parasit Vectors 2025）。三個數字擺埋一齊就明白：貓蚤（狗身上最常見）發育可行範圍係 13–35°C、濕度 50–92%（Trends Parasitol 2024）；要蚤全階段凍死，環境溫度要連續幾日低於 3°C（Merck）；而香港最凍嘅 1 月，平均最低仍有 14.6°C、全年平均濕度 70–83%（香港天文台）。即係話「凍死蚤」嘅條件喺香港唔會出現——蚤患係全年風險。蜱同樣：離開宿主嘅時間全在植被，只要地面唔長時間結冰，部分蜱種冬天仍活躍；衞生防護中心指本地斑疹熱個案大多有去植被地帶嘅歷史（行山徑、戶外工作地點、屋企附近植被地），風險以潮濕暖嘅春至秋季最高。（VCA；香港衞生防護中心）

蜱傳疾病：香港最需要認識嘅幾種

1. 巴貝斯蟲（Babesia gibsoni）＝ 香港「蜱熱」主角

香港狗最常見嘅節肢動物媒介感染，報告盛行率 3.7%，「懷疑蜱熱」病例中可高達 27%。一項 108 隻確診狗嘅研究顯示，最常見表現係食慾下降（67.6%）、黏膜變白（52.7%）、無精神（45.4%）、尿色異常（35.2%），約三成有發燒；108 隻中 98 隻（約九成）血小板低於參考範圍。最值得記住：只有 4.6% 主人報稱見過狗身上有蜱——冇見過唔等於冇被咬過。（Animals 2025）

2. 埃里希體／無形體，同斑疹熱

埃里希體急性期常見發燒、淋巴結同脾臟腫大、血小板低，亦可見唔食、行路僵硬、呼吸困難；慢性可流鼻血、大小便帶血、容易瘀。無形體病通常症狀極輕甚至無症狀，最常見異常係血小板下降。香港立克次體病以斑疹熱同恙蟲病最常見；斑疹熱由蜱傳播，潛伏期 6–15 日，可發燒、頭痛、肌肉痛、皮疹。衞生防護中心亦提醒，狗同老鼠身上都可以帶蜱。（Merck；香港衞生防護中心）

散步後檢查 + 拔蜱正確做法

蜱最愛陰暗、隱蔽、皮膚薄嘅位置：耳仔（耳廓內外、耳道口）、頸圈下、前腋下、胸口、腹部同腹股溝、腳趾之間、肛門周圍同尾根（VCA；PDSA）。未吸血嘅蜱細到似針頭或芝麻，吸血後脹到似綠豆甚至擦膠——所以唔止用眼睇，要用手指逐處摸。每次散步後兩分鐘就夠。

拔蜱要準備尖頭鑷子或蜱夾、手套、消毒用品，唔好用手。

  1. 撥開毛，貼近皮膚夾實蜱嘅口器位置，唔好夾住脹起嘅腹部。
  2. 穩定均勻嘅力：鑷子向直拉、唔好扭或猛扯（扯斷會令口器殘留）；用蜱夾就跟指示慢慢扭鬆，未鬆口都要繼續施壓，有時要一兩分鐘。
  3. 拔完用肥皂水清潔咬位、洗手；想保留蜱可放入密封、有酒精嘅容器。

三件唔好做：唔好擠壓蜱身（會令病原同唾液被擠入傷口）；唔好用火燒、塗凡士林或油、用酒精汽油刺激佢鬆口——唔會令蜱自行脫落，反而可能令口器殘留同增加傳播，各地衞生機構一致唔建議；唔好徒手拔（部分蜱傳病可經皮膚破損或黏膜感染）。若見到黑色小點留喺皮膚、咬位紅腫發熱有分泌物，或狗狗之後無精神，就見獸醫。（VCA；Asia Pac Allergy 2019；PDSA）

蚤：點知狗狗身上有蚤？

蚤糞測試：梳出黑褐色似塵嘅細粒放喺濕紙巾上——溶解並散出紅褐色就係蚤糞，唔溶唔變色多數只係泥塵。痕同甩毛集中喺尾根、臀部同大腿係蚤過敏性皮膚炎嘅典型位置。一隻雌蚤一日可產最多 50 粒卵、一生約 2,000 粒，生命週期由 12 日至 350 日——所以狗身上清乾淨，屋企仲可以有。（VCA；Merck）

預防選項概覽（唔講劑量）

  • 滴頸（spot-on）：滴喺頸背、隨皮膚擴散；有啲一個月一次，有啲維持幾個月。
  • 口服咀嚼片／錠：有啲同時覆蓋蜱，有啲只覆蓋蚤。
  • 頸圈：有啲係驅蜱型，適合高風險地區或成日撿蜱嘅狗。
  • 噴劑、粉劑：輔助或短期產品。

重點係邊款覆蓋蜱、邊款只覆蓋蚤，加上狗狗年齡、體重、健康狀況同家中其他動物——最好問獸醫幫你揀。兩個期望要管理：冇產品可以百分百阻止蜱埋身，有用蜱藥嘅狗蜱通常喺 24–48 小時內死亡掉落，但已足夠傳播部分病原，所以照樣要每日檢查同拔；產品亦唔係「即殺」，有啲蚤可生存 6–24 小時先死。（VCA；PDSA；Merck）

家居環境係另一半：洗狗床毛毯，吸塵集中狗瞓嘅位置、沙發同椅嘅縫隙、地板縫（蚤幼蟲怕光）；戶外集中處理陰涼潮濕位置，唔需要全個花園噴。嚴重感染通常要 6 星期至 3 個月先控制到；衞生防護中心亦建議定期為寵物同寵物床鋪做防蟲處理。（Merck；香港衞生防護中心）

幾時要即刻見獸醫

  • 發燒、無精神、唔食（蜱熱最常見三個表現）。
  • 牙肉、眼白或耳仔內側變白；尿色變深；無故瘀斑、流鼻血、大小便見血。
  • 行路僵硬、突然唔肯行；拔蜱後咬位紅腫發熱，或口器殘留。

呢啲要靠驗血、血清學或 PCR 確診，肉眼分唔到，亦唔應該自己俾人用藥或剩餘抗生素。三個最常見錯誤：「冇見過蜱所以冇事」（香港 108 隻病例只有 4.6% 主人報稱見過）、用手捏或火燒或塗油、只在夏天做預防。（Merck；Animals 2025）

Short answer: fleas and ticks are two different problems — fleas make dogs itch and damage the skin, while ticks transmit disease (in Hong Kong, mainly babesiosis or "tick fever"). Hong Kong is warm and humid, so neither is summer-only, and a two-minute full-body check after every walk is the most effective step you can take.

Ticks vs fleas

Ticks are arachnids with eight legs; fleas are wingless insects with six. Flea bites itch and can cause flea allergy dermatitis; heavy infestations (especially in puppies) cause anaemia from blood loss, plus tapeworms. A tick attaches firmly and can go unnoticed for days, and it transmits several pathogens: Babesia, Ehrlichia, Anaplasma and rickettsiae — which is why ticks matter more. Hard ticks also spend over 90% of their lifetime off the host, waiting in grass for an animal to brush past. (VCA; Merck)

Hong Kong: why prevention runs all year

Hong Kong's subtropical monsoon climate favours vectors (Parasit Vectors 2025). Three published numbers tell the story: the cat flea — most common on dogs — develops at 13–35°C and 50–92% humidity (Trends Parasitol 2024); killing fleas at every life stage needs below 3°C for several days (Merck); and Hong Kong's coldest month, January, still averages a daily minimum of 14.6°C, with year-round humidity of 70–83% (Hong Kong Observatory). Those flea-killing conditions never arrive here, so flea risk is year-round — and ticks are the same, since they live in vegetation and some species stay active in winter while the ground is not frozen. The Centre for Health Protection notes most local spotted fever cases had a history of visiting vegetated areas, with risk highest in the warm, humid spring-to-autumn months. (HK Centre for Health Protection; VCA)

Tick-borne disease: what to know in Hong Kong

1. Babesia gibsoni — the local "tick fever"

Babesiosis is the most common arthropod-borne infection in Hong Kong dogs: reported prevalence 3.7%, up to 27% among dogs investigated for suspected tick fever. In 108 confirmed cases, the commonest signs were reduced appetite (67.6%), pallor (52.7%), lethargy (45.4%) and abnormal urine colour (35.2%), with fever in about a third; 98 of 108 (about 90%) had platelets below the reference range. The detail worth remembering: only 4.6% of owners had ever seen a tick on their dog — never finding one does not mean your dog was never bitten. (Animals 2025)

2. Ehrlichia, Anaplasma and spotted fever

Acute ehrlichiosis causes fever, enlarged lymph nodes and spleen, and low platelets, and can also show as poor appetite, stiffness or difficulty breathing; long-term cases can bring nosebleeds, blood in urine or faeces and easy bruising. Anaplasmosis is usually mild or completely silent, with a platelet drop as the commonest abnormality. In Hong Kong the commonest rickettsial diseases are spotted fever and scrub typhus; spotted fever is tick-borne, incubates over 6–15 days, and causes fever, headache, muscle pain and rash. (Merck; HK Centre for Health Protection)

The post-walk check, and how to remove a tick

Ticks prefer dark, hidden, thin-skinned spots: the ears (inside and out, and the ear canal opening), under the collar, the front armpits, the chest, the belly and groin, between the toes, and around the anus and tail base (VCA; PDSA). An unfed tick is pinhead or sesame-seed sized and swells to pea or pencil-eraser size — so do not just look, run your fingers over every one of those spots after every walk.

To remove a tick, have fine-tipped tweezers or a tick-twisting tool, gloves and disinfectant ready — never bare fingers.

  1. Part the fur and grip the tick as close to the skin as possible, at the mouthparts — not by the swollen abdomen.
  2. Use steady, even pressure: with tweezers pull straight out, without twisting or jerking (which can snap off mouthparts); with a twisting tool, follow the instructions, twist gently, and keep the pressure on even if it does not release immediately — it can take a minute or two.
  3. Clean the bite area with soap and water and wash your hands; you can keep the tick in a sealed container with alcohol for identification.

Three things not to do: do not squeeze the tick's body (pressure can push pathogens and saliva into the wound); do not burn it, smother it with petroleum jelly or oil, or douse it with alcohol or petrol — these do not make a tick detach and may leave mouthparts behind, which is why health authorities advise against them; and do not use bare hands. If you see a small black dot left in the skin, a bite site that is red, hot or discharging, or later lethargy, see your vet. (VCA; Asia Pac Allergy 2019; PDSA)

Fleas: how to tell

The flea dirt test: comb out dark brown, dust-like specks onto a damp paper towel — dissolved into a reddish-brown smear means flea faeces; specks that stay solid are just dirt. Itching and hair loss at the tail base, rump and thighs is the classic flea allergy pattern. One female flea lays up to 50 eggs a day and about 2,000 in her life, with a life cycle of 12 to 350 days — which is why the dog can look clean while the home is not. (VCA; Merck)

Prevention options at a glance (no dosing advice)

  • Spot-on products: applied at the back of the neck and spread over the skin — some monthly, some lasting several months.
  • Oral chewables or tablets: some cover ticks as well as fleas, some cover fleas only.
  • Collars: some are tick-repellent, useful in high-risk areas or for dogs that constantly pick ticks up.
  • Sprays and powders: supporting or short-term measures.

The point is which product covers ticks and which only covers fleas, along with your dog's age, weight, health and other pets — so ask your vet to choose. Two expectations to manage: no product stops every tick attaching, and with an effective tick product ticks usually die and drop off within 24–48 hours — still long enough to transmit pathogens, so keep checking daily; and products are not instant-kill (fleas can survive and bite for 6–24 hours). (VCA; PDSA; Merck)

The home is the other half: wash bedding, vacuum where the dog sleeps and in sofa and floorboard crevices (flea larvae avoid light), and outdoors target shaded, damp spots rather than the whole yard. A heavy infestation usually takes 6 weeks to 3 months to control. (Merck) (Merck; HK Centre for Health Protection)

When to see a vet promptly

  • Fever, lethargy or going off food — the three commonest tick fever signs.
  • Gums, eye whites or ear insides turning pale; dark urine; unexplained bruising, nosebleeds, or blood in urine or faeces.
  • Stiffness or refusing to walk; a bite site that is red, hot or discharging after removal, or retained mouthparts.

These need blood tests, serology or PCR — not something to judge by eye or treat with human medicines or leftover antibiotics. The three commonest mistakes: "I have never seen a tick, so we are fine" (only 4.6% of owners in the Hong Kong case series had), squeezing or burning or greasing the tick, and doing prevention only in summer. (Merck; Animals 2025)

title: 狗狗無故瘦咗點算？體重下降嘅成因同紅旗警號
title_en: Dog Losing Weight for No Reason? Causes and Red Flags
desc_en: Unexplained weight loss in dogs is a symptom, not ageing. Learn to track it at home (BCS 1-9, monthly weight log), the classic causes with their warning-sign clusters, and the red flags that need a vet.
content_html:
一句話重點：冇開始過減肥、餐單同運動量都冇變，體重卻一直跌，係一個症狀，唔係「老咗正常」。跌超過正常體重一成（10%）而唔係脫水引起，屬臨床上重要嘅變化，值得驗血驗尿搵原因。

分清「有計劃減重」同「無故變瘦」

有計劃嘅減肥，跌磅係預期之內，但速度要有譜：一般每星期安全跌體重嘅 1–2%，至少每兩星期磅一次；跌得更快，可能係熱量減得太狠或者有健康問題。冇減肥計劃就要問：食量有冇靜靜雞減少（分糧、其他寵物偷食、換糧）、運動量有冇突然增加、生活有冇大變？壓力同環境改變係會令體重跌，但通常唔會持續、亦唔會跌好多。

家居追蹤三步

1. 同一部磅、同一時段、每月記錄。單次數字冇乜用，趨勢才有用；唔肯定，可以每幾日磅一次連續兩星期，帶記錄見獸醫。

2. 體態評分（BCS 1–9）。理想係 4 至 5 分：肋骨摸得到但睇唔到，從上望有腰，從側望腹部上收。1 分＝肋骨、腰椎、骨盆骨遠望已見；3 分＝肋骨容易摸到、骨盆骨開始突出；7 分＝肋骨要用力才摸到、腰唔明顯。

3. 肌肉狀況（睇脊骨同髖部）。摸脊柱兩側、肩胛、頭骨、兩邊盆骨頂；流失通常最先出現在脊柱兩側，分正常至嚴重四級。肥嘅狗都可以有明顯肌肉流失，所以體態同肌肉要分開評。

常見成因：睇「警號組合」

  • 牙痛／口腔問題：唔想食乾糧、食得慢、掉食物、流口水、唔肯俾人摸嘴邊。
  • 腸胃病／吸收不良：腹瀉超過三星期或反覆發作、嘔。「食好多但照瘦」係典型；胰臟外分泌不足（EPI）亦屬呢類，靠驗血（TLI）確診。
  • 糖尿病：飲多、尿多、食得多但體重照跌。
  • 腎病：早期飲多尿多；後期食慾差、嘔、牙肉蒼白、口氣臭、口腔潰瘍。
  • 內分泌問題要分方向：狗嘅甲狀腺功能低下典型係「食慾冇增、體重上升」；Addison's disease 會瘦、嘔、虛弱、飲多尿多。
  • 寄生蟲：幼犬最常見；肚仔脹（pot-bellied）可能提示腸道寄生蟲。
  • 癌症：體重跌同肌肉流失可以好慢，亦可以好突然。
  • 心臟病：咳、耐力下降；269 隻心衰竭狗嘅研究中，48.3% 出現肌肉流失。
  • 壓力／環境改變：換糧、搬屋、加新寵物；通常唔會持續跌、亦唔會跌得多。

紅旗：以下情況唔好等

  • 無故跌超過正常體重一成，或者短期內明顯變瘦（越跌得快越要緊）。
  • 食慾正常甚至增加，體重仍然持續下降。
  • 飲水同排尿明顯增加，或者開始唔願飲水。
  • 腹瀉超過三星期、反覆嘔、黑色柏油狀糞便、腹部脹大。
  • 口氣突然變臭、流口水、口腔潰瘍、牙肉蒼白、脊骨兩側肌肉凹落去。

獸醫會做咩？

  1. 問病史——食咩、食幾多、食慾同飲水大小便有冇變。
  2. 由鼻到全身檢查——磅重、評體態同肌肉、聽心臟肺、摸腹部、檢查口腔。
  3. 檢查——先做全血細胞計數（CBC）、血清生化、尿液分析、糞便寄生蟲檢查；有需要再驗 TLI、Addison's、照 X 光或超聲波、抽吸或活檢、心臟檢查。帶埋體重記錄去，比講「好似瘦咗」有用。

三個唔好做嘅事

  1. 唔好只係加肥、加零食、加蛋白質。如果係吸收唔到，或者糖尿病／腎病令營養流失，食多咗唔會補返，反而可能令腹瀉更差、亦遮蓋病情。
  2. 唔好當係「老咗正常」。老年狗肌肉自然減少（sarcopenia）會令體重輕微下降，但明顯跌就一定要檢查。
  3. 唔好自己俾補品、荷爾蒙藥或人用藥物。未確診前自行用藥會遮蓋徵狀，亦可能影響之後嘅檢查。

（食幾多同營養標準屬體重管理嘅題目；「飲水多、尿多」屬排尿變化嗰篇。）

content_html_en:
Short answer: if nothing about your dog's food or exercise has changed, weight loss is a symptom, not old age. Losing more than 10% of normal body weight — and not through dehydration — is clinically significant and warrants bloodwork and a urine test.

Planned weight loss vs unexplained weight loss

On a real weight-loss plan, losing weight is expected — but speed matters. Dogs on a plan can safely lose about 1–2% of body weight per week and should be weighed at least every two weeks; faster than that can mean calories were cut too hard, or that something medical is going on. With no diet in place, ask: has the amount eaten actually dropped (split meals, another pet stealing food, a food switch)? Has exercise increased? Has life changed (a move, a new pet)? Stress does cause weight loss, but it is rarely persistent or significant.

Three-step home tracking

1. One scale, same time of day, monthly log. A single number means little — the trend does. If you are unsure whether your dog is really losing weight, weigh every few days for two weeks and take the log to your vet.

2. Body condition score (BCS 1–9). Ideal is 4 or 5: ribs felt but not seen, a waist from above, a tucked abdomen from the side. 1 = ribs, lumbar vertebrae and pelvic bones visible from a distance; 3 = ribs easily felt, pelvic bones becoming prominent; 7 = ribs hard to feel, no visible waist.

3. Muscle condition — spine and hips. Feel the spine, scapulae, skull and hip points; loss shows first along the spine and is graded normal to severe. Overweight dogs can still lose significant muscle, so score body and muscle condition separately.

Classic causes: read the warning-sign cluster

  • Dental pain or mouth problems: refusing dry food, chewing slowly, dropping food, drooling, hating the muzzle being touched.
  • Gut disease or malabsorption: diarrhoea over three weeks or recurring, plus vomiting. Weight loss despite a good or ravenous appetite is the hallmark; exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (EPI) fits here and is confirmed by a TLI blood test.
  • Diabetes: drinking more, peeing more, eating more — and still losing weight.
  • Kidney disease: early on, drinking and peeing more; later, poor appetite, vomiting, pale gums, bad breath, mouth ulcers.
  • Endocrine problems — mind the direction: hypothyroidism in dogs usually causes weight gain without an increased appetite; Addison's disease causes weight loss with vomiting, weakness and more thirst and urination.
  • Parasites: common, especially in puppies; a pot-bellied look can hint at intestinal worms.
  • Cancer: weight loss and muscle wasting, gradual or very sudden.
  • Heart disease: coughing and poor exercise tolerance; of 269 dogs with congestive heart failure, 48.3% had muscle loss.
  • Stress or environment change: a new food, a move, a new pet; rarely persistent or significant.

Red flags: do not wait these out

  • Unexplained loss of more than 10% of normal body weight, or a fast, noticeable drop.
  • Appetite normal or increased, yet weight keeps falling.
  • Drinking and peeing clearly more than usual, or suddenly drinking less.
  • Diarrhoea beyond three weeks, repeated vomiting, black tarry stools, a bloated abdomen.
  • New bad breath, drooling, mouth ulcers, pale gums, visible muscle loss along the spine.

What the vet will do

  1. History — what you feed and how much, plus changes in appetite, thirst and toilet habits.
  2. Nose-to-tail examination — weight, body and muscle condition, heart, lungs, abdomen, mouth.
  3. Tests — blood count, serum biochemistry, urinalysis and faecal parasite testing first; then TLI, Addison's testing, X-rays or ultrasound, biopsy or heart checks as needed. Take a weight log with you.

Three things not to do

  1. Do not just add fat, treats or protein. If nutrients are not being absorbed, or are lost through diabetes or kidney disease, more food will not fix it — it can worsen diarrhoea and blur the picture.
  2. Do not write it off as ageing. Older dogs do lose muscle naturally (sarcopenia), but a noticeable weight drop still needs investigating.
  3. Do not self-treat with supplements, hormones or human medicines — it masks signs and can interfere with the tests your vet needs.

Our companion pieces cover feeding standards and nutrition ratios, and the urinary changes to watch.

title: 狗狗嘔黃色膽汁、白色泡？顏色解碼同求醫時機
title_en: Dog Vomiting Yellow Bile or White Foam? Colour Decoder and When to See a Vet
desc_en: Why dogs throw up yellow bile, white foam or clear liquid: a colour decoder, early-morning bilious vomiting syndrome, the red flags that mean an emergency (bloat/GDV, blood), what to do at home and what tests vets run.
content_html:
一句話重點：顏色係線索，唔係診斷。黃綠色泡多數係膽汁（多見於空肚、尤其清晨）；白色泡係口水混住吞落嘅空氣；有血即刻求醫。最危險係乾嘔嘔唔出＋肚脹硬，可能係胃扭轉。

顏色解碼

  • 黃／黃綠色泡——膽汁。伊利諾大學獸醫學院指膽汁呈黃或綠色、有時帶泡，胃空時最常見。
  • 白色泡——口水混住吞落嘅空氣，胃空或胃部受刺激時常見。
  • 透明水狀——水加胃液、口水；透明唔等於輕微。
  • 食物——食得太快、食完即運動、胃排空慢。
  • 有血——紅色、黑色或「咖啡渣」狀；PDSA：即刻聯絡獸醫。

Merck 獸醫手冊指咳嗽、呼吸困難更常見於「反流」而唔係嘔吐；若係咳完嘔白泡，方向可能係呼吸道或心臟。嘔吐會有腹部用力同前奏（流口水、舔嘴），反流係被動、食完即刻發生（VCA）。

清晨空肚嘔黃色：膽汁性嘔吐綜合症

若狗狗反覆清晨嘔膽汁，其他一切正常，獸醫會考慮呢個綜合症：膽汁由腸道回流到胃刺激黏膜而嘔，靠排除其他病因診斷（伊利諾大學獸醫學院）。常見情況係一日一餐、或最後一餐喺傍晚，但獸醫強調餵食時間表唔係「引起」呢個病。

方向係頻密小餐、睡前小食，必要時由獸醫處方胃酸抑制劑、促蠕動藥或胃黏膜保護劑（JAAHA 2016）。⚠️ 該研究 20 宗個案中 12 隻治療後改善，但有 3 宗最後發現病因係胃腺癌、飲食不當同肝病——唔可以自己認咗呢個診斷。

仲有咩常見原因？

  • 飲食不當、寄生蟲（VCA、PDSA）。
  • 異物／腸道阻塞——VCA 指常見而可以致命；Cornell 指屬急症、通常要手術（玩具、襪、石頭、粟米芯、骨頭）。
  • 胰臟炎——VCA：嘔吐、發燒、精神差、腹痛、肚瀉、食慾下降，可由高脂一餐觸發。
  • 腸胃炎／感染、肝腎病、荷爾蒙病（Merck、VCA），以及藥物反應或誤食人用藥——人用消炎止痛藥（ibuprofen、naproxen、aspirin）安全範圍極窄（VCA）。

紅旗：唔好等，即刻去獸醫

  1. 乾嘔嘔唔出＋肚脹硬——可能係胃扭轉（GDV），即時致命急症。VCA：腹部腫脹左側最明顯、輕敲肋骨後有鼓聲，亦會流口水、呼吸困難、虛脫；100 磅以上嘅狗一生約 20% 風險，即使較簡單個案死亡率仍達 10%–45%。
  2. 嘔吐物有血，或持續嘔吐超過 24–48 小時。
  3. 同時肚瀉＋精神差／脫水——PDSA：肚瀉超過 2–3 日、血便、腹痛、脫水（牙肉黏、眼窩凹）。
  4. 懷疑食咗異物或有毒物品、發燒、食慾全無、虛脫（VCA）。

家居可以做嘅事

  • 充足清水，小量多次咁飲（PDSA）；唔好自己斷水——Merck：除非正接受皮下或靜脈輸液，否則唔應限水。
  • 讓狗狗休息、暫停散步；嘔吐停咗之後，獸醫通常建議小份易消化、低脂低纖食物，再慢慢回復正常糧（PDSA、VCA）。
  • 做記錄（次數、時間、顏色、之前食過咩）；唔好自己俾人用藥——止嘔藥會遮蓋病情（VCA）。

VCA 指好多急性嘔吐會喺 24 小時內自己好轉，Merck 指少於 3–4 日、冇其他異常嘅短期嘔吐通常冇大礙。界線：只嘔一兩次、精神正常、肯飲水、冇血、冇肚脹 → 可觀察；一有紅旗就唔好等。

獸醫會做咩檢查？

  • 問病歷＋身體檢查（含腹部觸診）——VCA：有時已足以縮窄範圍，例如緊張又痛嘅腹部要懷疑胰臟炎。
  • 驗血、驗尿、驗糞便及 X 光——Merck：大部分嘔吐嘅狗都適合照，可揪出吞落嘅異物；需要時再做超聲波、內窺鏡＋切片或探查手術。

點樣減少復發？

  • 分餐、控制每餐份量——JAAHA 2004（1,634 隻狗、106 宗 GDV）：每餐份量大嘅狗風險明顯上升，無論一日食幾多餐。
  • 減慢食速（VCA 列為 GDV 風險因素）；唔好俾檯面食物同高脂食物。
  • 空肚嘔膽汁——伊利諾大學獸醫學院建議試睡前小食，或由獸醫評估轉處方飲食。
  • 收好藥物、垃圾、襪、繩、骨頭、粟米芯；定期驅蟲、按時接種（VCA、Cornell、PDSA）。

參考文獻

  1. VCA Animal Hospitals — Vomiting in Dogs；Bloat (GDV) in Dogs；Pancreatitis in Dogs；Testing for Vomiting；Ingestion of Foreign Bodies in Dogs；Common Over-the-Counter Toxins in Dogs.
  2. Merck Veterinary Manual — Vomiting in Dogs（2024）；PDSA — Vomiting in dogs（2024）；University of Illinois College of Veterinary Medicine — Bilious Vomiting Syndrome（2025）；Cornell Riney Canine Health Center — GDV；GI foreign body obstruction in dogs.
  3. JAAHA 2016 — Bilious Vomiting Syndrome in Dogs: 20 Cases（PubMed 27008323）；JAAHA 2004 — Diet-related risk factors for GDV（PubMed 15131099）.
content_html_en:
Short answer: colour is a clue, not a diagnosis. Yellow-green froth is usually bile (empty stomach, usually mornings); white foam is saliva and swallowed air; blood means see a vet now. Retching with a hard, swollen belly may be bloat (GDV).

Colour decoder

  • Yellow / green froth — bile; most common on an empty stomach (University of Illinois).
  • White foam — saliva plus swallowed air; common with an empty, irritated stomach.
  • Clear / watery — water, stomach fluid, saliva; clear does not mean mild.
  • Food — eating too fast, exercise after meals, slow stomach emptying.
  • Blood — red, black or 'coffee grounds' look; PDSA says call your vet now.
  • Coughing first? Merck: coughing or breathing trouble points to regurgitation, not vomiting.

Early-morning bile: bilious vomiting syndrome

Repeated early-morning bile in an otherwise normal dog suggests this syndrome: bile refluxes back from the intestines and irritates the stomach lining; it is diagnosed by ruling out other causes (University of Illinois). The schedule — one meal a day, or an early last meal — does not cause it.

Management: frequent small meals and a late-evening snack, plus vet-prescribed acid reducers or prokinetics if needed (JAAHA 2016). Of 20 reviewed cases 12 improved, but 3 had gastric adenocarcinoma, dietary indiscretion or liver disease.

Other common causes

  • Dietary indiscretion, parasites (VCA; PDSA).
  • Foreign body / obstruction — potentially life-threatening and usually needing surgery (VCA; Cornell).
  • Pancreatitis — vomiting, fever, lethargy, abdominal pain, diarrhoea; a fatty meal can trigger it (VCA).
  • Gastroenteritis, infection, liver or kidney disease, hormonal disease (Merck); also medication reactions and human NSAIDs such as ibuprofen, which have a very narrow safety margin in dogs (VCA).

Red flags: see a vet now

  1. Unproductive retching with a hard, swollen belly — possible GDV (bloat), life-threatening. Per VCA the swelling is most obvious on the left side and may sound drum-like; dogs over 100 lb have roughly a 20% lifetime risk, and even uncomplicated cases carry a 10%–45% mortality rate.
  2. Blood in the vomit, or continuous vomiting beyond 24–48 hours.
  3. Vomiting with diarrhoea plus lethargy or dehydration — PDSA: diarrhoea over 2–3 days, blood, a painful abdomen, sticky gums.
  4. Suspected foreign body or toxin, fever, no appetite, collapse (VCA).
  5. Home watch: many acute cases settle within 24 hours (VCA); any red flag means don't wait.

What to do at home

  • Fresh water, little and often (PDSA); never withhold water yourself unless your vet says so (Merck).
  • Rest and skip walks; once vomiting stops, vets usually suggest small amounts of a digestible, low-fat, low-fibre food before returning to the normal diet (PDSA; VCA).
  • Keep a log (how often, when, colour, what they ate) and give no human medication — anti-nausea drugs can mask the cause (VCA).

What your vet will check

  • History and physical exam, including abdominal palpation — sometimes enough to narrow things down (VCA).
  • Blood, urine and faecal tests plus X-rays; ultrasound, endoscopy or exploratory surgery if a foreign body is suspected (Merck; VCA).

Preventing recurrence

  • Split meals and control portions — a larger volume per meal significantly raised GDV risk regardless of meals per day (JAAHA 2004).
  • Slow the eating down (a GDV risk factor per VCA); skip table scraps and fatty food.
  • Empty-stomach bile — try a small late-night meal, or discuss a prescription diet (University of Illinois).
  • Store medicines, bins, socks, string, bones and corn cobs out of reach.

References

  1. VCA Animal Hospitals — Vomiting in Dogs; Bloat (GDV) in Dogs; Pancreatitis in Dogs; Testing for Vomiting; Ingestion of Foreign Bodies in Dogs; Common Over-the-Counter Toxins in Dogs.
  2. Merck Veterinary Manual — Vomiting in Dogs; PDSA — Vomiting in dogs; University of Illinois College of Veterinary Medicine — Bilious Vomiting Syndrome; Cornell Riney Canine Health Center — GDV and GI foreign body obstruction; JAAHA 2016 (PubMed 27008323); JAAHA 2004 (PubMed 15131099).
